### 2. Full TOML for Reference Channels

#### `dot_config/television/cable/mlflow.toml`
```toml
[metadata]
name = "mlflow"
description = "MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models (file/sqlite/http backends)"
requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]

[source]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models",
]
display = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  ({split:\\t:4})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
no_sort = true

[preview]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full    | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view metrics | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
]
header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"

[ui]
input_header = "MLflow"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open-or-drill"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"
ctrl-b = "actions:open-browser"
alt-r = "actions:drill-runs"
alt-j = "actions:dump-json"

[actions.open-or-drill]
description = "Drill into experiment runs / open JSON detail"
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
  __hint__) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
  *[!0-9]*) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
  *) MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" ;;
esac"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-id]
description = "Copy row id to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.open-browser]
description = "Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only)"
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; uri="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"; case "$uri" in http://*|https://*) ;; *) printf '[open-browser] needs MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http(s)://…\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$id" in __hint__) printf '[open-browser] no row selected\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; url="$uri/"; if [ "${#id}" = "32" ] && printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/0/runs/$id"; elif printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/$id"; else url="$uri/#/models/$id"; fi; if command -v open >/dev/null; then open "$url"; elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null; then xdg-open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 & elif command -v wslview >/dev/null; then wslview "$url"; else printf '[open-browser] no opener\\n'; sleep 2; fi"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.drill-runs]
description = "Re-launch tv scoped to experiment"
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
  __hint__|*[!0-9]*) printf '[drill-runs] not an experiment row\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;;
esac
MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" """
mode = "execute"

[actions.dump-json]
description = "Print full JSON detail to terminal"
command = "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
```

**Key patterns here:**
- **Multiple sources** (Ctrl+S cycling): `command` is a list of shell commands
- **Preview cycling** (Ctrl+F): `command` is also a list (each cycle is a different preview)
- **Helper scripts** (`mlflow-source.py`, `mlflow-preview.py`): Deployed in `~/.config/television/`
- **Piping to colorizers**: `| bat --color=always --plain --paging=never` for JSON; `| jq -C` for JSON in other channels
- **Custom actions** with `mode = "execute"` for blocking operations, `mode = "fork"` for non-blocking
- **`no_sort = true`**: Preserve helper script's output order (important for cycling sources with semantics)
- **Clipboard abstraction**: Reusable `_clip()` function handles pbcopy/wl-copy/xclip/OSC 52

#### `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml`
```toml
[metadata]
name = "fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]

[source]
command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:connect"
alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-s = "actions:status"
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:pueue"

[actions.connect]
description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.status]
description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"
command = "fleet chezmoi status --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.info]
description = "fleet info for this host"
command = "fleet info --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.pueue]
description = "fleet pueue for this host"
command = "fleet pueue --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
```

**Key patterns here:**
- **Simple source command**: Single shell command (no cycling)
- **Preview delegates to CLI**: `fleet hosts --describe` — not a helper script
- **Alt+ namespace**: Avoids tmux/TV conflicts (convention across mac-apps, linux-apps, ssh-config)
- **Multiple Alt-actions**: Each invokes a different fleet subcommand
- **Consistent output format**: Tab-delimited with `{split:\t:N}` placeholders for action substitution

#### `dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl`
```toml
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
[metadata]
name = "mac-apps"
description = "macOS apps — graceful quit / restart / activate / hide via Apple Events"
requirements = []

[source]
command = """osascript -e 'tell application "System Events"' -e 'set out to ""' -e 'repeat with p in (every application process whose background only is false)' -e 'set out to out & (unix id of p) & tab & (name of p) & linefeed' -e 'end repeat' -e 'return out' -e 'end tell' 2>/dev/null"""
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:1}"

[preview]
command = [
  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'
ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command 2>/dev/null
echo
lsappinfo info "$pid" 2>/dev/null | head -30""",
  """name='{split:\\t:1}'
. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh 2>/dev/null
printf 'App: %s\\n' "$name"
if appresponsive "$name" 2>/dev/null; then
  printf 'Status: responsive\\n'
else
  printf 'Status: NOT responding\\n'
fi
printf '\\n(2s Apple Event timeout)\\n'""",
]
header = "{split:\\t:1}  (pid {split:\\t:0})"

[ui]
input_header = "macOS Apps"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:activate"
alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]
alt-r = ["actions:restart", "reload_source"]
alt-h = "actions:hide"
alt-k = ["actions:force-kill", "reload_source"]
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:probe"

[actions.activate]
description = "Bring app to front"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appactivate '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.quit]
description = "Graceful Quit (⌘Q-equivalent Apple Event)"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appquit '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.restart]
description = "Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && apprestart '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.hide]
description = "Hide app windows"
command = """osascript -e 'on run argv' -e 'tell application "System Events" to set visible of (first process whose name is (item 1 of argv)) to false' -e 'end run' -- '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.force-kill]
description = "SIGKILL by PID"
command = "kill -9 '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.info]
description = "Detail pager: ps + full lsappinfo"
command = """pid='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:1}'; { printf '=== %s (pid %s) ===\\n\\n' "$name" "$pid"; ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command; printf '\\n'; lsappinfo info "$pid"; } 2>/dev/null | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "Probe app responsiveness"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && name='{split:\\t:1}' && (appresponsive "$name" 5 && printf '%s: responsive\\n' "$name" || printf '%s: NOT responding\\n' "$name"); sleep 2"""
mode = "execute"
{{ end -}}
```

**Key patterns here:**
- **Chezmoi template** (`.tmpl`): Gated with `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}` so it only renders on macOS
- **Keybindings with multiple actions**: `alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]` chains an action with a TV built-in command
- **Source-helper function**: `. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh` sources a shell helper file that defines `appactivate`, `appquit`, `apprestart`, `appresponsive`
- **Inline Apple Events**: Direct `osascript` for one-off verbs (hide) to keep channel self-contained

#### `dot_config/television/cable/linux-apps.toml.tmpl`
```toml
{{- if and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") -}}
[metadata]
name = "linux-apps"
description = "Linux apps — graceful quit / restart / activate via gtk-launch + pkill"
requirements = []

[source]
command = """sh -c '. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh 2>/dev/null && applist --pids' 2>/dev/null"""
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:1}"

[preview]
command = [
  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'
name='{split:\\t:1}'
ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,comm 2>/dev/null
echo
printf '=== child processes ===\\n'
pgrep -P "$pid" -af 2>/dev/null | head -10
echo
printf '=== full command line ===\\n'
tr '\\0' ' ' < "/proc/$pid/cmdline" 2>/dev/null | head -c 500
echo""",
  """name='{split:\\t:1}'
. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh 2>/dev/null
printf 'App: %s\\n' "$name"
if appresponsive "$name" 2>/dev/null; then
  printf 'Status: responsive\\n'
else
  printf 'Status: NOT responding (or hung / not running / no MPRIS handle)\\n'
fi""",
]
header = "{split:\\t:1}  (pid {split:\\t:0})"

[ui]
input_header = "Linux Apps"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:activate"
alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]
alt-r = ["actions:restart", "reload_source"]
alt-k = ["actions:force-kill", "reload_source"]
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:probe"

[actions.activate]
description = "Bring app to front"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh && appactivate '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.quit]
description = "Graceful Quit (SIGTERM via app's pkill pattern)"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh && appquit '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.restart]
description = "Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh && apprestart '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.force-kill]
description = "SIGKILL by PID"
command = "kill -9 '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.info]
description = "Detail pager: ps + pgrep tree + cmdline"
command = """pid='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:1}'; { printf '=== %s (pid %s) ===\\n\\n' "$name" "$pid"; ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command 2>/dev/null; printf '\\n=== child processes ===\\n'; pgrep -P "$pid" -af 2>/dev/null; printf '\\n=== full command line ===\\n'; tr '\\0' ' ' < "/proc/$pid/cmdline" 2>/dev/null; printf '\\n'; } 2>/dev/null | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "Probe app responsiveness (MPRIS-only)"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh && name='{split:\\t:1}' && (appresponsive "$name" 5 && printf '%s: responsive\\n' "$name" || printf '%s: NOT responding\\n' "$name"); sleep 2"""
mode = "execute"
{{ end -}}
```

**Key patterns here:**
- **Cross-platform Alt-key mirroring**: Same keybindings (alt-q, alt-r, alt-k, etc.) as mac-apps, but different implementation
- **Template gating**: `{{- if and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") -}}` gates to Linux with profile check
- **Shared interface contract**: Same `appactivate`, `appquit`, `apprestart`, `appresponsive` function names (defined in `56_linux_apps.sh`), different innards

### 3. TOML Schema Fields Across All Channels

| Section | Field | Type | Purpose | Examples |
|---------|-------|------|---------|----------|
| `[metadata]` | `name` | string | Channel identifier (used in `tv <name>`) | `mlflow`, `fleet-hosts` |
| | `description` | string | One-liner shown in `tv channels` and help | `"MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models"` |
| | `requirements` | array | CLI tools this channel needs (informational) | `["mlflow", "uv"]`, `["fleet", "ssh"]` |
| `[source]` | `command` | string or array | Shell command(s) to generate rows; array = Ctrl+S cycling sources | `"fleet hosts --list-tsv"` or array of commands |
| | `display` | string | How to format row for display (uses `{split:\t:N}` placeholders) | `"{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"` |
| | `output` | string | What gets piped to actions (uses `{split:\t:N}` placeholders) | `"{split:\\t:0}"` (just the ID) |
| | `watch` | float | Auto-refresh interval in seconds; omit for manual-only | `2.0`, `5.0` |
| | `no_sort` | boolean | Preserve command's output order (important for semantic cycling) | `true` (mlflow, pueue) |
| `[preview]` | `command` | string or array | Shell command(s) to generate preview pane; array = Ctrl+F cycling | `"fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"` or array |
| | `header` | string | Title line for preview pane | `"{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:2})"` |
| `[ui]` | `input_header` | string | Picker title (top-left) | `"MLflow"`, `"Super Productivity"` |
| `[ui.preview_panel]` | `size` | integer | Preview pane width (chars) | `60` |
| `[keybindings]` | keys | string or array | Bind key to action name or chain with TV built-ins | `"enter = "actions:connect""` or `["actions:quit", "reload_source"]` |
| `[actions.NAME]` | `description` | string | Help text for the action | `"SSH into the selected fleet host"` |
| | `command` | string | Shell command to execute (uses `{split:\t:N}` for substitution) | `"ssh '{split:\\t:1}'"` |
| | `mode` | string | `"execute"` (blocking, user sees output) or `"fork"` (non-blocking) | `"execute"` for SSH, `"fork"` for quick commands |

**Placeholder syntax:**
- `{split:\t:N}` — Split row by tabs, extract column N (0-indexed)
- `{split: :N}` — Split row by spaces, extract column N
- Whitespace matters: `{split:\\t:0}` is escaped tab, `{split: :0}` is space

### 4. Rclone in This Repo

**Installation:**
- **Ansible role**: `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` installs rclone via Homebrew (macOS) and custom shell download script (Linux)
- **Listed in docs**: `dot_config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md` (invocation: `rclone `, description: `"Sync files to/from cloud storage"`)
- **Not yet in TV**: No existing `rclone.toml` channel

**Current rclone coverage:**
- Installed system-wide as a CLI tool
- No TV channel yet; users currently run `rclone` directly in terminal
- `rclone` command is already listed in the tools markdown for Alt+T access

---

### 5. Schema Fields Actually Used Across Channels

**Always present:**
- `[metadata]` with `name`, `description`
- `[source]` with `command`, `display`, `output`
- `[keybindings]` with at least one binding (usually `enter`)
- `[actions.*]` sections with `command` and `mode`

**Optional but common:**
- `[preview]` — most channels have it (some omit to reduce overhead)
- `[ui]` with `input_header` — helps with branding
- `[ui.preview_panel]` with `size` — useful for wide previews (JSON, config)
- `watch` — auto-refresh (pueue: 2s, super-productivity: 5s; most channels omit)
- `requirements` — metadata only; TV doesn't enforce it
- `no_sort = true` — only when cycling sources have semantic meaning (mlflow, pueue)
- Multiple preview `command` entries for Ctrl+F cycling

**Action patterns:**
- `mode = "execute"` — for SSH, pager, long-running tasks (user sees output)
- `mode = "fork"` — for quick side-effects (copy, kill -TERM, activate window)
- Keybindings can chain: `["actions:verb", "reload_source"]` to refresh after mutation

---

### 6. Helper Scripts and Backing Tools

**Python helpers** (in `~/.config/television/`):
- `mlflow-source.py` — Parses MLflow tracking backends (file, sqlite, http); implements source cycling
- `mlflow-preview.py` — Renders experiment/run/model JSON with `--view` (full, metrics)
- `super-productivity-source.sh` — Queries local REST API (http://127.0.0.1:3876)
- `agent-sessions.py` — Lists Claude Code agent panes

**Shell helpers** (in `~/.config/shell/`):
- `54_macos_apps.sh` — Defines `appactivate`, `appquit`, `apprestart`, `appresponsive` (Apple Events)
- `56_linux_apps.sh` — Defines same functions via gtk-launch, pkill patterns, MPRIS
- These are sourced by actions to keep channel TOML DRY

**CLI tools that channels shell out to:**
- `fleet` (custom umbrella CLI) — `fleet hosts --list-tsv`, `fleet hosts --describe`, `fleet chezmoi status`, etc.
- `lsof` / `ss` — Port listener enumeration (ports.toml)
- `pueue` — Task queue CLI (pueue.toml sources `pueue status --json`)
- `curl` + `jq` — Super Productivity REST API client
- `osascript` — Direct Apple Events (mac-apps inline, no helper needed)

---

### 7. Documentation to Read Before Writing rclone Channel

1. **`docs/tools/tv.md`** (already provided above) — General TV concepts, community channels, source/preview cycling, keybinding conventions
2. **`docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md`** — XDG layout, modular config patterns (relevant for where to place helper scripts)
3. **`docs/tools/cli-tools.md`** — How tools are catalogued (rclone is already there; your channel should complement this)
4. **`docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`** — Deep-dive on how fleet-hosts channel works (good reference for multi-action Alt-key pattern)
5. **`docs/tools/super-productivity.md`** — API integration patterns (if you want to source rclone remotes via API or config parsing)

No `docs/tools/television.md` or dedicated TOML schema doc exists; the channels themselves are the reference implementation.

---

### Recommendations for `dot_config/television/cable/rclone.toml`

Based on the patterns above, here's what a consistent rclone channel should look like:

**Likely structure:**
```toml
[metadata]
name = "rclone"
description = "rclone remotes: list, browse mounts, show stats"
requirements = ["rclone"]

[source]
command = [
  "rclone listremotes",           # Source 1: all remotes
  "rclone config dumpsecure",     # Source 2: config detail (JSON)
]
display = "{split: :0}"           # or parse JSON if using dumpsecure
output = "{split: :0}"

[preview]
command = "rclone about '{split: :0}' --json | jq -C . || rclone config show '{split: :0}'"

[ui]
input_header = "rclone Remotes"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:copy_remote"
alt-s = "actions:size_stats"      # rclone size (storage quota)
alt-b = "actions:browse"          # rclone lsf for listing
alt-m = "actions:mount_info"      # rclone mount status (if running)

[actions.copy_remote]
description = "Copy remote name to clipboard"
command = "_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z \"$d\" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' \"$d\" | pbcopy; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | _clip"
mode = "fork"

[actions.size_stats]
description = "Show remote size and quota"
command = "rclone about '{split: :0}' --json | jq -C . | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
```

**Key considerations:**
- Rclone has no native "drill-in" equivalent, so Ctrl+S cycling is less critical (maybe list remotes vs. config)
- Alt+S for size stats mirrors the `ssh-config` / `fleet-hosts` Alt-key convention
- Use `rclone --json` to output JSON, pipe to `jq -C` for color (like super-productivity)
- Helper script may not be needed (unlike mlflow, fleet); rclone CLI is self-contained
- Consider `watch = 0` (manual refresh only) — rclone remotes don't change frequently

19	# `mlruns/` dir picks file mode, otherwise it creates `mlruns/`. To pin a

22	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow

28	#                      Alt+R on an experiment row sets it and re-launches tv)

1	# Custom fleet-hosts channel for television (tv).
2	# Sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — the same inventory used by
3	# `fleet chezmoi apply` / `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` /
4	# `fleet exec`. Mirrors the `ssh-config` cable's UX but reads fleet's TOML
5	# inventory instead of ~/.ssh/config, so hosts with explicit
6	# hostname/user/port/identity_file (no ssh_alias) are reachable too.
7	#
8	# The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to:
9	#   fleet hosts --list-tsv      (source — `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` lines)
10	#   fleet hosts --describe N    (preview pane content)
11	#   fleet hosts N               (Enter action — os.execvp("ssh", ...))
12	# So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes
13	# automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync).
14	#
15	# Usage:
16	#   tv fleet-hosts
17	#   fleet hosts          # same picker via the fleet umbrella
18	#   fleet hosts lab-box  # skip the picker, SSH directly
19	#
20	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
21	#   Enter      SSH into the selected host
22	#   Alt+T      BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login actually work?)
23	#   Alt+S      fleet chezmoi status scoped to this host
24	#   Alt+I      fleet info scoped to this host
25	#   Alt+P      fleet pueue scoped to this host
26	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
27	#
28	# `local = true` hosts are intentionally hidden — they live on the
29	# orchestrator and have no SSH endpoint. Run `fleet hosts --list-tsv
30	# --include-local` to confirm one is in the inventory.

50	alt-t = "actions:probe"

52	alt-i = "actions:info"

58	mode = "execute"
59

```text
1	{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
2	# mac-apps channel — macOS GUI app control via Apple Events
3	#
4	# Pick a foreground GUI app, then choose a lifecycle action. Defaults are
5	# safe: Enter brings the app to front; destructive actions are Alt-gated.
6	#
7	# Pairs with: dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl (sourced by every action
8	#             to reuse appactivate / appquit / apprestart / appresponsive)
9	#             dot_config/television/cable/mac-procs.toml.tmpl (process picker,
10	#             sorted by compressed-aware memory — for profiling, not control)
11	#             dot_config/television/cable/kill-process.toml (cross-platform
12	#             process killer; default Enter = SIGTERM, no Apple Events)
13	#
14	# Why a separate channel from mac-procs / kill-process:
15	#   - kill-process Enter = SIGTERM — destructive for apps with state
16	#     (OrbStack VMs, Docker daemons, Slack drafts, unsaved buffers).
17	#   - mac-procs Enter = passthrough — for analysis, not lifecycle.
18	#   - mac-apps Enter = activate — non-destructive default; graceful Quit
19	#     is one Alt-key away and uses Apple Events so apps tear down cleanly.
20	#
21	# Usage:
22	#   tv mac-apps
23	#
24	# Keybindings:
25	#   Enter      Activate (bring to front)
26	#   Alt+Q      Graceful Quit (⌘Q-equivalent Apple Event) + reload
27	#   Alt+R      Quit + poll until gone + relaunch + reload
28	#   Alt+H      Hide app windows (System Events visible=false)
29	#   Alt+K      Force kill by PID (SIGKILL; last resort) + reload
30	#   Alt+I      Info pager: ps + full lsappinfo dump
31	#   Alt+P      Probe responsiveness (5s Apple Event timeout)
32	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (metadata <-> responsiveness)
33	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
34	#
35	# Why Alt+ rather than Ctrl+: tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner
36	# apps. See CLAUDE.md "Keybinding" cross-file rule.
37	
38	[metadata]
39	name = "mac-apps"
40	description = "macOS apps — graceful quit / restart / activate / hide via Apple Events"
41	requirements = []
42	
43	[source]
44	# AppleScript exposes (unix id, name) for foreground GUI apps in one query.
45	# `background only is false` filters out daemons / agents / loginwindow etc.
46	# Output is "<pid>\t<name>\n" — matches `applist --pids` from the shell
47	# helper, but inlined so this channel works even before chezmoi-apply
48	# deploys the helper file.
49	command = """osascript -e 'tell application "System Events"' -e 'set out to ""' -e 'repeat with p in (every application process whose background only is false)' -e 'set out to out & (unix id of p) & tab & (name of p) & linefeed' -e 'end repeat' -e 'return out' -e 'end tell' 2>/dev/null"""
50	display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
51	# Default stdout when piping `tv mac-apps | ...` is the app NAME — what
52	# every helper (appquit/applaunch/appactivate/apprestart) wants on argv.
53	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
54	
55	[preview]
56	# Cycle 1: ps + lsappinfo. Fast (<50 ms).
57	# Cycle 2: responsiveness probe. ~2s per render — opt-in via Ctrl+F.
58	command = [
59	  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'
60	ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command 2>/dev/null
61	echo
62	lsappinfo info "$pid" 2>/dev/null | head -30""",
63	  """name='{split:\\t:1}'
64	. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh 2>/dev/null
65	printf 'App: %s\\n' "$name"
66	if appresponsive "$name" 2>/dev/null; then
67	  printf 'Status: responsive\\n'
68	else
69	  printf 'Status: NOT responding (or hung)\\n'
70	fi
71	printf '\\n(2s Apple Event timeout — false positives possible during launch)\\n'""",
72	]
73	header = "{split:\\t:1}  (pid {split:\\t:0})"
74	
75	[ui]
76	input_header = "macOS Apps"
77	
78	[keybindings]
79	enter = "actions:activate"
80	alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]
81	alt-r = ["actions:restart", "reload_source"]
82	alt-h = "actions:hide"
83	alt-k = ["actions:force-kill", "reload_source"]
84	alt-i = "actions:info"
85	alt-p = "actions:probe"
86	
87	[actions.activate]
88	description = "Bring app to front (Alt+Tab equivalent)"
89	command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appactivate '{split:\\t:1}'"""
90	mode = "fork"
91	
92	[actions.quit]
93	description = "Graceful Quit (⌘Q-equivalent Apple Event)"
94	command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appquit '{split:\\t:1}'"""
95	mode = "fork"
96	
97	[actions.restart]
98	description = "Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch"
99	# `execute` (not `fork`) because apprestart polls for up to 15s; we want
100	# the user to see "still quitting…" if it takes a moment.
101	command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && apprestart '{split:\\t:1}'"""
102	mode = "execute"
103	
104	[actions.hide]
105	description = "Hide app windows (System Events visible=false)"
106	# Inlined rather than reusing the helper file because the shell helper
107	# doesn't expose `hide` as a function — only the four lifecycle verbs.
108	command = """osascript -e 'on run argv' -e 'tell application "System Events" to set visible of (first process whose name is (item 1 of argv)) to false' -e 'end run' -- '{split:\\t:1}'"""
109	mode = "fork"
110	
111	[actions.force-kill]
112	description = "SIGKILL by PID (last resort; bypasses Apple Event)"
113	# Uses PID column, not name. Apps with multiple processes (Chrome Helper,
114	# Electron renderers) only have their main process listed in `applist`,
115	# so SIGKILL here kills the parent — children are reaped by launchd.
116	command = "kill -9 '{split:\\t:0}'"
117	mode = "fork"
118	
119	[actions.info]
120	description = "Detail pager: ps + full lsappinfo"
121	command = """pid='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:1}'; { printf '=== %s (pid %s) ===\\n\\n' "$name" "$pid"; ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command; printf '\\n'; lsappinfo info "$pid"; } 2>/dev/null | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
122	mode = "execute"
123	
124	[actions.probe]
125	description = "Probe app responsiveness (5s Apple Event timeout)"
126	command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && name='{split:\\t:1}' && (appresponsive "$name" 5 && printf '%s: responsive\\n' "$name" || printf '%s: NOT responding\\n' "$name"); sleep 2"""
127	mode = "execute"
128	{{ end -}}
129
```
</details></tool-use>

2	# linux-apps channel — Linux GUI app control via gtk-launch + pkill -TERM
3	#
4	# Linux counterpart to dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl.
5	# Pick a running GUI app (registered or auto-derived from .desktop scan),
6	# then choose a lifecycle action. Same keybindings as mac-apps where the
7	# verb exists on both sides — Alt+H is mac-only by design (Linux can't
8	# hide windows without compositor IPC).
9	#
10	# Pairs with: dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl (sourced by every
11	#             action to reuse appactivate / appquit / apprestart /
12	#             appresponsive — and by [source] to drive `applist --pids`)
13	#             ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf (user override file; lets
14	#             users register per-app pkill patterns for AppImage/snap/
15	#             Flatpak apps that auto-derivation can't resolve correctly)
16	#
17	# Coverage caveats (mirrors backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md):
18	#   - appactivate falls back to applaunch unless the GNOME window-calls
19	#     extension is installed; documented as best-effort.
20	#   - appresponsive only meaningful for apps registered with --mpris=NAME
21	#     (Spotify, mpv, VLC, …); for Electron/Firefox apps it degrades to
22	#     apprunning + stderr note. No public Linux API analog to macOS
23	#     Apple Events' `with timeout`.
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   tv linux-apps
27	#
28	# Keybindings:
29	#   Enter      Activate (bring to front — best-effort without window-calls)
30	#   Alt+Q      Graceful Quit (pkill -TERM via app's pkill pattern) + reload
31	#   Alt+R      Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch + reload
32	#   Alt+K      Force kill by PID (SIGKILL; last resort) + reload
33	#   Alt+I      Info pager: ps + pgrep details
34	#   Alt+P      Probe responsiveness (MPRIS-only; stderr note otherwise)
35	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (metadata <-> responsiveness)
36	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
37	#
38	# Why Alt+ rather than Ctrl+: tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner
39	# apps. See CLAUDE.md "Keybinding" cross-file rule.
40	
41	[metadata]

44	requirements = []
45	
46	[source]
47	# Source the helper (which also sources ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf
48	# to populate the user's overrides), then emit `<pid>\t<name>` for each
49	# running app the helper recognises. Output format matches mac-apps for
50	# preview / display / output split consistency.
51	command = """sh -c '. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh 2>/dev/null && applist --pids' 2>/dev/null"""

53	# Default stdout when piping `tv linux-apps | ...` is the app NAME — what

55	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
56	
57	[preview]
58	# Cycle 1: ps + pgrep tree. Fast (<50 ms).
59	# Cycle 2: responsiveness probe — MPRIS-only meaningful response.
60	command = [
61	  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'
62	name='{split:\\t:1}'
63	ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,comm 2>/dev/null
64	echo
65	printf '=== child processes ===\\n'

67	echo
68	printf '=== full command line ===\\n'
69	tr '\\0' ' ' < "/proc/$pid/cmdline" 2>/dev/null | head -c 500
70	echo""",

75	  printf 'Status: responsive\\n'
76	else

78	fi

80	]
81	header = "{split:\\t:1}  (pid {split:\\t:0})"
82	
83	[ui]

85

88	alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]

97	mode = "fork"

1	# Super Productivity channel for television (tv).
2	# Read-only browser for tasks, projects and tags via SP's local REST API
3	# (http://127.0.0.1:3876, exposed by the desktop Electron app).
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   tv super-productivity
7	#
8	# Prerequisites (one-time):
9	#   1. Super Productivity desktop ≥ 18.0.0 (the Local REST API was added in
10	#      upstream PR #6981, first shipped 2026-03-26). The Brewfile cask gets
11	#      the latest, but if you have an older install pinned, run:
12	#        brew upgrade --cask super-productivity
13	#      Confirm with: defaults read "/Applications/Super Productivity.app/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString
14	#   2. In the app: Settings → Misc → enable "Local REST API"
15	#      (NOT in Sync & Export — that section only configures Dropbox/WebDAV/
16	#      SuperSync data sync, which is independent of the REST API.)
17	#   3. Restart the app
18	#
19	# Verify the API is up:
20	#   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3876/health | jq
21	#   # -> {"ok":true,"data":{"server":"up","rendererReady":true}}
22	#
23	# When the API is unreachable, this channel shows a single hint row instead
24	# of an empty list — so you always know whether SP is the problem or `tv` is.
25	#
26	# Reverse-engineered route reference + design rationale:
27	#   docs/tools/super-productivity.md
28	#
29	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
30	#   1. Active tasks      open tasks excluding done (▶ marks current)
31	#   2. All active tasks  open + done tasks (✓ marks done)
32	#   3. Archived tasks    moved-to-archive tasks
33	#   4. Projects          all projects with task counts
34	#   5. Tags              all tags
35	#
36	# Preview cycle (Ctrl+F):
37	#   1. Full task JSON (jq-pretty)
38	#   2. Notes only (tspin-highlighted when tailspin is installed)
39	#
40	# Keybindings (read-only by design — no mutations in v0.1):
41	#   Enter      Open full JSON detail in pager
42	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy task ID to clipboard (overrides TV default)
43	#   Alt+Y      Copy task title to clipboard
44	#   Alt+J      Dump full JSON to terminal
45	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview
46	#   Ctrl+O     Toggle preview panel
47	#   Ctrl+S     Cycle source
48	#
49	# Refresh: every 5s (less aggressive than pueue's 2s — task data changes
50	# slowly and the renderer round-trip is heavier than a local CLI call).
51	#
52	# NOTE on Phase 2 (mutations): start/stop/complete/archive via Alt-keys is
53	# intentionally deferred until the read-only flow proves stable. The REST
54	# API supports them today (POST /tasks/:id/start, POST /task-control/stop,
55	# PATCH /tasks/:id with {isDone:true}, POST /tasks/:id/archive).
56	
57	[metadata]
58	name = "super-productivity"
59	description = "Super Productivity (read-only): browse tasks, projects, tags via local REST API"
60	requirements = ["curl", "jq"]
61	
62	[source]
63	command = [
64	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-active",
65	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-all",
66	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-archived",
67	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh projects",
68	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tags",
69	]
70	display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  [{split:\\t:2}]  {split:\\t:3}"
71	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
72	watch = 5.0
73	no_sort = true
74	
75	[preview]
76	# GET /tasks/:id only resolves for task ids — for project/tag rows the curl
77	# returns 404 and we fall back to a friendly message. Same for the down-API
78	# hint row (id "0"). All API responses are wrapped in {ok, data} — extract
79	# .data for display. Use `jq -C` for built-in syntax coloring (single binary,
80	# avoids `bat` PATH/TTY-detection gotchas inside TV's preview process).
81	command = [
82	  "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -C .data || echo 'No JSON detail for this row (project/tag entries do not have a /tasks/:id endpoint, or API is unreachable).'",
83	  "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.data.notes // \"(no notes)\"' || echo '(no notes available)'",
84	]
85	header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"
86	
87	[ui]
88	input_header = "Super Productivity"
89	
90	[ui.preview_panel]
91	size = 60
92	
93	[keybindings]
94	enter = "actions:open-detail"
95	# Override TV global ctrl-y (which copies the full display line) with id-only copy
96	ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
97	alt-y = "actions:copy-title"
98	alt-j = "actions:dump-json"
99	
100	[actions.open-detail]
101	description = "Open full JSON detail in pager"
102	command = "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -C .data | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
103	mode = "execute"
104

```text
1	# Custom listening ports cable channel for television (tv)
2	# Shows all listening TCP/UDP ports with PID, process name, and address.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   tv ports
6	#
7	# Keybindings:
8	#   Enter      Show process details
9	#   Ctrl+K     Kill the selected process (stays in picker to kill more)
10	#   Ctrl+D     Force kill (kill -9)
11	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
12	#
13	# Preview shows full process details via `ps`.
14	# Cross-platform: uses lsof (macOS) or ss (Linux).
15	
16	[metadata]
17	name = "ports"
18	description = "Listening ports: PID, process, address"
19	
20	[source]
21	command = """
22	if command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
23	  lsof -i -P -n 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN | awk '{printf "%-6s  %-20s  %s\\n", $2, $9, $1}' | sort -u
24	elif command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
25	  ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | awk '{
26	    addr=$4; pid=$7;
27	    gsub(/.*pid=/,"",pid); gsub(/,.*$/,"",pid);
28	    gsub(/.*users:\\(\\("/,"",pid);
29	    printf "%-6s  %-20s  %s\\n", pid, addr, $7
30	  }' | sort -u
31	fi
32	"""
33	
34	[preview]
35	command = "ps -p '{split: :0}' -o pid,ppid,%cpu,%mem,etime,command 2>/dev/null"
36	
37	[keybindings]
38	enter = "actions:details"
39	ctrl-k = ["actions:kill", "reload_source"]
40	ctrl-d = ["actions:force_kill", "reload_source"]
41	
42	[actions.details]
43	description = "Show full process details"
44	command = "ps -p '{split: :0}' -o pid,ppid,user,%cpu,%mem,etime,command; echo '---'; lsof -i -P -n -p '{split: :0}' 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN"
45	mode = "execute"
46	
47	[actions.kill]
48	description = "Kill the selected process"
49	command = "kill '{split: :0}'"
50	mode = "fork"
51	
52	[actions.force_kill]
53	description = "Force kill (SIGKILL)"
54	command = "kill -9 '{split: :0}'"
55	mode = "fork"
56
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# television (tv) Quick Reference
2	
3	[television](https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television) — blazing-fast TUI fuzzy finder with pluggable "channels".
4	
5	Custom channels: `dot_config/television/cable/` (chezmoi-managed)
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Basic Usage
10	
11	```bash
12	tv                   # Open interactive picker (default channel)
13	tv <channel>         # Open a specific channel, e.g. tv sesh
14	tv list-channels     # List all available channels
15	tv --help            # List all flags
16	```
17	
18	From tmux: `prefix + T` opens the sesh channel as a popup (see [Tmux Integration](#tmux-integration)).
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Community Channels
23	
24	tv has a built-in channel package manager. Run once after install (and periodically to update):
25	
26	```bash
27	tv update-channels
28	```
29	
30	This downloads [community-maintained channels](https://alexpasmantier.github.io/television/community/channels-unix) into `~/.config/television/cable/`. It:
31	
32	- **Skips** channels whose requirements aren't met on your system (e.g. `apt-packages` on macOS)
33	- **Skips** channels that already exist (won't overwrite custom channels)
34	- Covers git, docker, k8s, brew, cargo, GitHub, sesh, tmux, and many more
35	
36	Notable community channels: `sesh`, `git-branch`, `git-log`, `git-stash`, `git-diff`, `brew-packages`, `docker-containers`, `gh-issues`, `gh-prs`, `just-recipes`, `zoxide`, `zsh-history`, `env`, `dirs`, `files`, `text`.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Custom Channels
41	
42	### `tools` channel
43	
44	Parses `~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md` at runtime (deployed via chezmoi from `dot_config/docs/tools/`). The markdown file is the single source of truth — edit it to add or update tools.
45	
46	Open with `tv tools` or `prefix + U` in tmux.
47	
48	| Key | Action |
49	|-----|--------|
50	| `Enter` | Execute selected tool immediately |
51	| `Ctrl+/` | Toggle preview panel (tldr or `--help`) |
52	
53	For pasting an invocation to the shell buffer (with trailing space for tools that need arguments), use the fzf ZLE widget instead: **Alt+T** in any zsh session.
54	
55	---
56	
57	### `lan-devices` channel
58	
59	Fuzzy-search devices on the local subnet with open ports, MAC/vendor, hostname (rDNS + mDNS), ping RTT, and last-seen timestamp. Backed by `~/.config/television/lan-scan.sh`, which writes results incrementally to `~/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv` and per-host nmap detail to `~/.cache/tv/lan-ports/<ip>.txt`. The channel uses `watch = 2.0`, so rows stream into the picker as the background scan progresses (state column: `discovered` → `scanning` → `scanned`).
60	
61	Open with `tv lan-devices`, or run a synchronous scan first with the `lanscan` shell alias.
62	
63	**Sudo-gated with fallback:** when passwordless sudo is available (`sudo -n true`), the script uses `arp-scan -lgq` for the richest MAC/vendor data. Otherwise it falls back to `nmap -sn` ping sweep + OS ARP cache (`arp -an` on macOS, `ip neigh` on Linux). Vendor lookup for the fallback path uses nmap's `nmap-mac-prefixes` OUI database.
64	
65	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
66	
67	| Source | Description |
68	|--------|-------------|
69	| All devices | Every discovered host, sorted by IP (default) |
70	| With open ports | Only rows whose port count is ≥ 1 |
71	| Fresh only | Hosts seen within the last 5 minutes |
72	
73	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
74	
75	1. Cached nmap service detail (fast, from `~/.cache/tv/lan-ports/<ip>.txt`)
76	2. Live `nmap -sV -Pn -F` rescan (blocking, ~10–30 s)
77	3. ARP + rDNS + mDNS + ping metadata
78	
79	**Keybindings** (`Alt+` namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts):
80	
81	| Key | Action |
82	|-----|--------|
83	| `Enter` | Full `nmap -sV -A` in execute mode |
84	| `Alt+R` | Rescan ports on selected host + reload |
85	| `Alt+F` | Rescan full subnet (discover + ports) + reload |
86	| `Alt+D` | Re-discover only (no port scan) + reload |
87	| `Alt+S` | SSH to selected host |
88	| `Alt+H` | Open `http://<ip>` in the system browser |
89	| `Alt+C` | Clear scan cache + reload |
90	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy IP to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH) |
91	
92	**Cache layout:**
93	
94	```
95	~/.cache/tv/
96	├── lan-devices.tsv         # one row per device (watched by tv)
97	├── lan-ports/<ip>.txt      # nmap -sV output per host
98	├── lan-scan.log            # scan progress log
99	└── lan-scan.lock/          # mutex directory (removed on exit)
100	```
101	
102	Requires `nmap`; `rustscan` and `arp-scan` are used when present (all part of the `networking_tools` ansible role).
103	
104	---
105	
106	### `logs` channel
107	
108	Fuzzy-browse log files on the machine with colorful previews. Open with `tv logs`.
109	
110	Source file: [`dot_config/television/cable/logs.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/television/cable/logs.toml.tmpl) (chezmoi template — the journalctl cycle below is only rendered on Linux). Full toolbelt writeup: [log-tools.md](log-tools.md).
111	
112	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
113	
114	1. Project-local logs under `$PWD` — `.log` / `.ndjson` / `.jsonl` via `fd -HI`
115	2. User + system log dirs — `~/.cache/**/*.log`, `~/Library/Logs` on macOS, `/var/log/*.log` / `syslog*` / `messages*` (readable only)
116	3. **Linux only** — `journalctl --output=short-iso -n 2000` for systemd journal recent lines. Templated out on macOS because journalctl output lines are not file paths and the preview/Enter/Alt+T actions can't act on them (a dedicated `tv journalctl` channel would be the follow-up).
117	
118	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
119	
120	1. Colorful tail via [`tailspin`](https://github.com/bensadeh/tailspin) — `tail -n 500 FILE | tspin --print`; falls back to raw `tail` when `tspin` is missing
121	2. Plain [`bat`](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat) view — `bat --style=plain --color=always --line-range=:500` for unbiased comparison
122	
123	**Keybindings:**
124	
125	| Key | Action |
126	|-----|--------|
127	| `Enter` | Open in `lnav` (falls back to `ccze -A \| less -R`, then plain `less -R`) |
128	| `Alt+T` | Follow with `tspin --follow` (or `tail -F \| tspin --print` on older tailspin) |
129	| `Alt+E` | Open in `$EDITOR` |
130	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy file path to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH) |
131	
132	Requires `fd` (part of the `base` ansible role). Tailspin, lnav, ccze are part of `devtools`.
133	
134	---
135	
136	### `services` channel
137	
138	Cross-platform fuzzy picker for systemd services (Linux) and launchd jobs (macOS), with tailspin-colored log previews and Alt-key lifecycle actions. Open with `tv services`.
139	
140	Source file: [`dot_config/television/cable/services.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/television/cable/services.toml.tmpl) (chezmoi template — Linux and macOS get different `systemctl` vs `launchctl` bodies). Full writeup including symbol legend and sudo caveats: [services.md](services.md).
141	
142	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
143	
144	1. Running only — active services, system + user merged
145	2. All loaded — active + inactive + failed among runtime-known units
146	3. Failed only — crashed / non-zero exit
147	4. User-scope only — `systemctl --user` / macOS `gui/$UID/` domain
148	5. **Installed on-disk** — every unit file / `.plist` on disk, with enablement badges (`✓ Enabled` / `○ Disabled` / `— Static` / `⊘ Masked` on Linux; `● Loaded` / `○ On-disk` on macOS). This is the "configured but not enabled" discovery view — land on a `○ Disabled` row, hit `Alt+L`, done.
149	
150	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
```

1	# Custom SSH config channel for television (tv)
2	# Parses Host entries from ~/.ssh/config AND ~/.ssh/config.d/* (Include support).
3	# The community ssh-hosts channel only reads ~/.ssh/config directly.
4	#
5	# Each entry shows which file the host is defined in, so duplicates across
6	# config.d/* are easy to spot. The output (what gets passed to ssh / actions)
7	# is just the bare hostname.
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   tv ssh-config
11	#
12	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
13	#   Enter      SSH into selected host
14	#   Alt+T      Online probe: BatchMode=yes test (does pubkey login actually work?)
15	#   Alt+A      Offline batch scan: list every host + whether a local key file exists
16	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
17	#
18	# Preview shows resolved config via `ssh -G` plus a local-key existence check
19	# (no network — just stat the IdentityFile paths).
20	
21	[metadata]
22	name = "ssh-config"
23	description = "SSH hosts (with Include config.d/* support)"
24	requirements = ["ssh", "awk", "sort"]
25	
26	[source]
27	# Emit "<source-file>\t<hostname>" so the picker shows the origin file but
28	# actions still receive a clean hostname via {split:\t:1}.
29	command = """
30	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
31	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
32	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
33	  awk -v src="$rel" '
34	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
35	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
36	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
37	      }
38	    }' "$f"
39	done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2
40	"""
41	display = "{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:0})"
42	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
43	
44	[preview]
45	command = """
46	host='{split:\\t:1}'
47	src='{split:\\t:0}'
48	echo "# defined in: $src"
49	echo
50	ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(host|hostname|user|port|identityfile|proxycommand|proxyjump|forwardagent|identityagent|localforward|remoteforward)[[:space:]]'
51	echo
52	echo '--- local key check (offline) ---'
53	found=0
54	while IFS= read -r f; do
55	  [ -z "$f" ] && continue
56	  case "$f" in '~/'*) f="$HOME/${f#'~/'}";; '~') f="$HOME";; esac
57	  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
58	    echo "  [OK]   $f"
59	    found=1
60	  else
61	    echo "  [miss] $f"
62	  fi
63	done <<EOF
64	$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
65	EOF
66	if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
67	  echo
68	  echo '  => no IdentityFile present locally — password login likely required'
69	  echo '     (or relies on ssh-agent / IdentityAgent — try Alt+T to probe)'
70	fi
71	"""
72	
73	[keybindings]
74	enter = "actions:connect"
75	alt-t = "actions:probe"
76	alt-a = "actions:scan_all"
77	
78	[actions.connect]
79	description = "SSH into the selected host"
80	command = "ssh '{split:\\t:1}'"
81	mode = "execute"
82	
83	[actions.probe]
84	description = "Probe selected host with BatchMode (no password prompt allowed)"
85	command = """
86	host='{split:\\t:1}'
87	echo "# Probing $host with BatchMode=yes (ConnectTimeout=3)"
88	echo "# Exit 0 = passwordless login works; non-zero = needs password / unreachable / key not authorized"
89	echo
90	ssh -o BatchMode=yes \\
91	    -o ConnectTimeout=3 \\
92	    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \\
93	    -o PreferredAuthentications=publickey,hostbased,gssapi-with-mic \\
94	    "$host" true
95	rc=$?
96	echo
97	case $rc in
98	  0)   echo "[OK] passwordless login works for '$host'" ;;
99	  255) echo "[FAIL] connection / auth error (exit 255) — needs password, key not authorized, or host unreachable" ;;
100	  *)   echo "[FAIL] remote command failed (exit $rc) — auth probably OK but 'true' failed" ;;
101	esac
102	echo
103	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
104	read -r _
105	"""
106	mode = "execute"
107	
108	[actions.scan_all]
109	description = "Offline scan: for every host, check if any IdentityFile exists locally"
110	command = """
111	echo "# Scanning all hosts (offline — no network) ..."
112	echo "# Legend: [OK] = at least one IdentityFile present locally"
113	echo "#         [--] = no key file on disk (password / agent / unconfigured)"
114	echo
115	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
116	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
117	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
118	  awk -v src="$rel" '
119	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
120	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
121	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
122	      }
123	    }' "$f"
124	done | sort -u -t '\t' -k2,2 | while IFS=$'\\t' read -r src host; do
125	  keyline=""
126	  found=0
127	  while IFS= read -r kf; do
128	    [ -z "$kf" ] && continue
129	    case "$kf" in '~/'*) kf="$HOME/${kf#'~/'}";; '~') kf="$HOME";; esac
130	    if [ -f "$kf" ]; then
131	      keyline="$kf"
132	      found=1
133	      break
134	    fi
135	  done <<EOF
136	$(ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^identityfile / {print $2}')
137	EOF
138	  if [ "$found" -eq 1 ]; then
139	    printf '  [OK] %-28s %-22s -> %s\\n' "$host" "($src)" "$keyline"
140	  else
141	    printf '  [--] %-28s %-22s    (no local key)\\n' "$host" "($src)"
142	  fi
143	done
144	echo
145	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
146	read -r _
147	"""
148	mode = "execute"
149

=== pueue.toml ===
# Pueue task manager channel for television (tv)
# Fuzzy-search pueue tasks, preview logs, and manage tasks interactively.
#
# Usage:
#   tv pueue
#
# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
#   1. All tasks (newest first)
#   2. Active only (Running + Queued + Paused)
#   3. Failed only
#   4. Groups overview
#
# Keybindings (Alt+key avoids conflicts with TV built-ins and tmux):
#   Enter      Follow running task / view finished task log / show group status
#   Alt+E      Edit task command (stashed/queued only, opens $EDITOR)
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy raw command to clipboard (overrides TV default; OSC 52 over SSH)
#   Alt+Y      Copy raw command to clipboard (same as Ctrl+Y)
#   Alt+A      Copy full `pueue add ...` command to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)
#   Alt+G      Filter by group (opens new tv with only that group's tasks)
#   Alt+P      Pause task
#   Alt+R      Resume (start) task
#   Alt+K      Kill task
#   Alt+T      Restart task (in-place)
#   Alt+X      Remove task
#   Alt+L      Clean all finished tasks
#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (log output / JSON details)
#   Ctrl+O     Toggle preview panel
#
# Auto-refreshes every 2 seconds via watch mode.

[metadata]
name = "pueue"
description = "Pueue task manager: search, preview logs, pause/resume/kill/restart"
requirements = ["pueue", "jq"]

[source]
command = [
  """pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.tasks | to_entries | sort_by(.value.id | tonumber) | reverse | .[].value | (if .status == "Queued" then "\u23f3 Queued" elif .status == "Stashed" then "\u23f9 Stashed" elif (.status | type == "object") then if (.status | has("Running")) then "\u25b6 Running" elif (.status | has("Done")) then if .status.Done.result == "Success" then "\u2713 Done" else "\u2717 Failed" end elif (.status | has("Paused")) then "\u23f8 Paused" else (.status | keys[0]) end else (.status | tostring) end) as $st | [(.id | tostring), $st, .group, .original_command] | @tsv'""",
  """pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.tasks | to_entries | sort_by(.value.id | tonumber) | reverse | .[].value | select(.status == "Queued" or (.status | type == "object" and (has("Running") or has("Paused")))) | (if .status == "Queued" then "\u23f3 Queued" elif (.status | has("Running")) then "\u25b6 Running" elif (.status | has("Paused")) then "\u23f8 Paused" else (.status | keys[0]) end) as $st | [(.id | tostring), $st, .group, .original_command] | @tsv'""",
  """pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.tasks | to_entries | sort_by(.value.id | tonumber) | reverse | .[].value | select(.status | type == "object" and has("Done") and .status.Done.result != "Success") | [(.id | tostring), "\u2717 Failed", .group, .original_command] | @tsv'""",
  """pueue group --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, .value.status, ("parallel=" + (.value.parallel_tasks | tostring))] | @tsv'""",
]
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  [{split:\\t:2}]  {split:\\t:3}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
watch = 2.0
no_sort = true

[preview]
# Preview cycle 1 pipes pueue log output through `tspin --print` when tailspin
# is installed, for colorful highlighting of timestamps/levels/IPs/URLs in the
# task log. Falls back to raw text on fresh installs (pre-devtools-role).
command = [
  "if command -v tspin >/dev/null 2>&1; then pueue log '{split:\\t:0}' --lines 200 2>/dev/null | tspin --print 2>/dev/null; else pueue log '{split:\\t:0}' --lines 200 2>/dev/null; fi || pueue log '{split:\\t:0}' 2>/dev/null || echo 'No log available for: {split:\\t:0}'",
  "pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq '.tasks[\"{split:\\t:0}\"] | del(.envs)' 2>/dev/null || echo 'No details for: {split:\\t:0}'",
]
header = "Task {split:\\t:0} ({split:\\t:1})"

[ui]
input_header = "Pueue Tasks"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 55

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:follow"
alt-e = "actions:edit"
# Override TV global ctrl-y (copies full display line) to copy just the command
ctrl-y = ["actions:copy_command", "reload_source"]
alt-y = ["actions:copy_command", "reload_source"]
alt-a = ["actions:copy_pueue_add", "reload_source"]
alt-g = "actions:filter_group"
alt-p = ["actions:pause", "reload_source"]
alt-r = ["actions:resume", "reload_source"]
alt-k = ["actions:kill", "reload_source"]
alt-t = ["actions:restart", "reload_source"]
alt-x = ["actions:remove", "reload_source"]
alt-l = ["actions:clean", "reload_source"]

[actions.follow]
description = "Follow running task, view log, or show group status"
=== kill-process.toml ===
# Kill process channel for television (tv)
# Raycast-style process killer: fuzzy search by name, see CPU/MEM, kill.
#
# Usage:
#   tv kill-process
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Kill the selected process (SIGTERM)
#   Ctrl+K     Kill and refresh list (stay in picker to kill more)
#   Ctrl+D     Force kill (SIGKILL) and refresh
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Sorted by memory usage (descending), like Raycast.
# Preview shows full process tree and open files.

[metadata]
name = "kill-process"
description = "Kill process: fuzzy search by name with CPU/MEM stats"

[source]
command = """
if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
  ps -eo pid,pcpu,pmem,rss,comm -m 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | awk '{
    pid=$1; cpu=$2; mem=$3; rss=$4;
    n=split($5,a,"/"); name=a[n];
    mb=rss/1024;
    printf "%-6s  %-30s  CPU %5s%%  MEM %6.0f MB\\n", pid, name, cpu, mb
  }'
else
  ps -eo pid,pcpu,pmem,rss,comm --sort=-rss 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | awk '{
    pid=$1; cpu=$2; mem=$3; rss=$4;
    n=split($5,a,"/"); name=a[n];
    mb=rss/1024;
    printf "%-6s  %-30s  CPU %5s%%  MEM %6.0f MB\\n", pid, name, cpu, mb
  }'
fi
"""

[preview]
command = "ps -p '{split: :0}' -o pid,ppid,user,pgid,%cpu,%mem,etime,command 2>/dev/null"

[keybindings]
enter = ["actions:kill", "reload_source"]
ctrl-k = ["actions:kill", "reload_source"]
ctrl-d = ["actions:force_kill", "reload_source"]

[actions.kill]
description = "Kill process (SIGTERM)"
command = "kill '{split: :0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.force_kill]
description = "Force kill (SIGKILL)"
command = "kill -9 '{split: :0}'"
mode = "fork"
=== channels.toml ===
# Cable channel: browse all tv channels with descriptions
#
# Usage:
#   tv channels
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Open selected channel in tv
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows the full TOML configuration for the selected channel.

[metadata]
name = "channels"
description = "Browse all available tv channels with descriptions"

[source]
command = """awk 'FILENAME!=prev{section=""; prev=FILENAME} /^\\[/{section=$0} section=="[metadata]" && /^name =/{name=$0; gsub(/.*= *"|"$/,"",name)} section=="[metadata]" && /^description =/{desc=$0; gsub(/.*= *"|"$/,"",desc); printf "%-30s │ %s\\n", name, desc}' ~/.config/television/cable/*.toml"""

[preview]
command = "bat -n --color=always ~/.config/television/cable/'{split: :0}'.toml 2>/dev/null || cat ~/.config/television/cable/'{split: :0}'.toml"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open"

[actions.open]
description = "Open selected channel in tv"
command = "tv '{split: :0}'"
mode = "execute"
=== tools.toml ===
# Custom tools cable channel for television (tv)
# Parses ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md at runtime — single source of truth.
#
# Usage:
#   tv tools                               (from shell)
#   prefix + U in tmux                     (popup)
#   Alt+T in zsh                           (opens fzf ZLE variant instead)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Execute selected tool immediately
#   Ctrl+T     Show tldrf page (multi-language fallback) in terminal
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows tldr page (zh_TW → zh → en fallback) or --help output.

[metadata]
name = "tools"
description = "CLI tools quick-launch: select a tool to execute it"
requirements = ["awk"]

[source]
command = """
awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
  inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
  desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
  printf "%-22s  %s\\n", inv, desc
}' ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md
"""

[preview]
command = """
tool=$(printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | sed 's/ *$//')
if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en "$tool" 2>/dev/null || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
else
  "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
fi
"""

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:exec"
ctrl-t = "actions:tldrf"

[actions.exec]
description = "Execute selected tool"
command = "{split: :0}"
mode = "execute"

[actions.tldrf]
description = "Show tldr page (multi-language fallback)"
command = "zsh -ic 'tldrf {split: :0}'"
mode = "execute"

1	# Config file conventions

3	A quick tour of the dotfile / config organisation patterns this repo

8	and [`tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](../tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). For
9	the shell-specific tier rule see
10	[`shells/architecture.md`](../shells/architecture.md).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## A. Where configs live
15	
16	### A1. XDG Base Directory Specification
17	
18	[freedesktop.org spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html);
19	the modern default. Four env vars carve up `$HOME` into purpose-tagged
20	subtrees:
21	
22	| Env var             | Default                | What goes there |
23	| ------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------- |
24	| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`  | `~/.config/`           | User config (this is where 90% of modern tools land) |
25	| `$XDG_DATA_HOME`    | `~/.local/share/`      | App data, tool installs (mise toolchains, oh-my-zsh, blesh, …) |
26	| `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`   | `~/.cache/`            | Disposable caches (zsh history search cache, bat cache, …) |
27	| `$XDG_STATE_HOME`   | `~/.local/state/`      | Runtime state (less critical than data; used less often) |
28	| `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`  | `/run/user/$UID/`      | Volatile, sub-second-scope IPC sockets (Linux only) |
29	
30	Tools that follow XDG (most modern ones): nvim, git, mise, starship,
31	zoxide, direnv, bat, eza, atuin, zellij, gh, fd, ripgrep.
32	
33	Tools that **don't** follow XDG (stuck for backwards-compat):
34	- bash (`~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`)
35	- zsh (`~/.zshrc` — but supports `ZDOTDIR` redirect)
36	- ssh (`~/.ssh/`)
37	- some older tools (`~/.tmux.conf`, `~/.gemrc`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.curlrc`)
38	
39	In this repo: `dot_config/{nvim,git,mise,starship,zoxide,direnv,bat,
40	eza,atuin,zellij,gh,fd,ripgrep,zsh,bash,shell}/` — XDG locations.
41	
42	### A2. Tool-specific dirs (pre-XDG)
43	
44	OpenSSH lives in `~/.ssh/` with strict 0700 perms. Bash insists on
45	`~/.bashrc` / `~/.bash_profile` at `$HOME`. tmux defaults to
46	`~/.tmux.conf` (newer versions also accept `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf`).
47	We follow each tool's actual lookup order rather than fighting it.
48	
49	In this repo: `dot_ssh/`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, `dot_zshrc.tmpl`,
50	`dot_gitconfig.tmpl` (also at `$HOME` — git 2.13+ also reads
51	`~/.config/git/config`, but `~/.gitconfig` is the classic canonical).
52	
53	### A3. Platform-specific dirs
54	
55	Some tools use OS-native dirs even on non-XDG:
56	
57	| OS       | Convention                                    |
58	| -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
59	| macOS    | `~/Library/Application Support/<App>/`        |
60	| Windows  | `%APPDATA%\<App>\`                            |
61	| Linux    | usually XDG; sometimes `~/.<app>/`            |
62	
63	In this repo: `Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/`
64	(macOS-only chezmoi templates; gated in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` per OS
65	to avoid creating phantom dirs on the other OS).
66	
67	---
68	
69	## B. How modular config is structured
70	
71	### B1. Single canonical file
72	
73	The simplest pattern: one rc file does everything.
74	Examples: `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.tmux.conf`.
75	
76	Pros: easy to read top-to-bottom, no load-order surprises.
77	Cons: grows unwieldy past ~500 lines; merge conflicts when multiple
78	sources contribute.
79	
80	### B2. `.d/` drop-in fragments
81	
82	Old sysadmin pattern from `/etc/` (`/etc/cron.d/`, `/etc/sudoers.d/`,
83	`/etc/profile.d/`, `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`). One canonical file +
84	a `.d/` directory; the tool loops over the dir and sources each
85	fragment alphabetically.
86	
87	User-side examples:
88	- `~/.ssh/config.d/*` (OpenSSH 7.3+; pulled in by `Include config.d/*`
89	  directive in `~/.ssh/config`)
90	- `~/.bashrc.d/*` (RHEL/Rocky/Alma/Fedora skel; their `~/.bashrc`
91	  loops over this dir)
92	- `~/.bash_completion.d/*` (less standard; some completion frameworks)
93	
94	Pros: drop a file → enabled. Each fragment is independent; a package
95	can ship one without modifying the canonical config.
96	Cons: order is glob-sort fragile (most use `NN_` prefixes). Tools
97	that don't natively support `.d/` need a manual loader.
98	
99	In this repo: `dot_ssh/private_config.d/` → `~/.ssh/config.d/*`,
100	included by `~/.ssh/config`. Plus `~/.bashrc.d/*` is sourced as a
101	user backward-compat layer in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` step 11 (NOT where
102	we place chezmoi-managed bash configs — see B3).
103	
104	### B3. Hybrid: XDG location + `.d`-style modular inside
105	
106	When a tool's canonical config doesn't natively support `.d/` but we
107	want the modular benefits: put modular files at the XDG location and
108	write our own loader.
109	
110	In this repo: `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/NN_*.{sh,zsh,bash}` —
111	sourced by a `load_modular_dir` function defined in
112	`dot_zshrc.tmpl` / `dot_bashrc.tmpl` that globs `*.<ext>` and sources
113	in alphabetical order. The `NN_` filename prefix controls load order.
114	
115	Why not just put these in `~/.bashrc.d/`? Because the skel's
116	`~/.bashrc.d` loop (on RHEL) runs from inside the original `~/.bashrc`
117	— after we replace that with our managed bashrc, that loop is gone.
118	Our own bashrc sources `~/.bashrc.d/*` at step 11 (after ble-attach),
119	which is too late for OMB plugin config or pre-init env. So managed
120	configs live in `~/.config/{shell,bash}/` (loaded mid-bashrc), and
121	`~/.bashrc.d/` is reserved for **user-dropped** files only.
122	
123	Full deep-dive: [`shells/architecture.md`](../shells/architecture.md).
124	
125	### B4. Plugin manager directories
126	
127	When a tool has a plugin manager (oh-my-zsh, oh-my-bash, tpm, lazy.nvim,
128	direnvrc), plugins live in a dedicated dir managed by the framework:
129	
130	- `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/<plugin>/` (OMZ; cloned via
131	  `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`)
132	- `~/.oh-my-bash/custom/plugins/<plugin>/` (OMB; same pattern)
133	- `~/.tmux/plugins/<plugin>/` (TPM)
134	- `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` + `~/.local/share/nvim/lazy/<plugin>/`
135	  (lazy.nvim — config in XDG_CONFIG_HOME, payloads in XDG_DATA_HOME)
136	
137	We don't fight these — let the framework own its dir, and clone
138	upstream plugins via `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` so chezmoi pulls
139	them weekly.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## C. User customisation layers (override patterns)
144	
145	These are escape hatches — places where users can stash machine-
146	local or experimental config without polluting chezmoi-managed files.
147	
148	### C1. `~/.foorc.local` include (the [include] directive pattern)
149	
150	Used when the canonical config supports an "include another file"
151	directive. The managed file ends with a conditional include of
152	`~/.foorc.local`; the local file is gitignored / chezmoi-ignored.
153	
154	Examples in this repo:
155	- `dot_gitconfig.tmpl` includes `~/.gitconfig.local` (per-machine
156	  `[safe]`, `[credential]`, `[http.proxy]`). Listed in
157	  `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` so chezmoi never tracks it. Silently
158	  no-ops when absent (git's `[include] path = ~/.gitconfig.local`
159	  is forgiving).
160	- `dot_ssh/dot_config` includes `~/.ssh/config.local` similarly.
161	
162	When to use: tool has native include directive AND the canonical
163	config has stable structure that won't break on partial overrides.
164	
165	### C2. `~/.foorc.adhoc` self-sourced tail (our chezmoi-ignored pattern)
166	
167	Used when there's no native include directive — we hand-roll one at
168	the end of the managed rc:
169	
170	```bash
171	# end of dot_zshrc.tmpl / dot_bashrc.tmpl
172	[ -r "$HOME/.zshrc.adhoc" ] && . "$HOME/.zshrc.adhoc"
173	```
174	
175	Auto-created on first apply with a header comment. Listed in
176	`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Sourced LAST so the user always wins on
177	conflict.
178	
179	When to use: shell rc files where we want a per-machine override
180	without forcing the user to learn chezmoi templates. See `dot_zshrc
181	.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` for the canonical examples.
182	
183	### C3. distro skel conventions (`~/.bash_aliases`, `~/.bashrc.d/*`)
184	
185	Files / dirs that distro `/etc/skel/` configs tell users to populate.
186	Not chezmoi-managed; we just source them for backward-compat so
187	existing user content survives our managed rc taking over.
188	
189	Examples:
190	- `~/.bash_aliases` — Debian / Ubuntu skel sources this; our managed
191	  bashrc step 11 also sources it.
192	- `~/.bashrc.d/*` — RHEL / Rocky / Alma / Fedora skel loops over it;
193	  our managed bashrc step 11 also loops.
194	- `~/.profile` / `~/.bash_profile` — login-shell entry; our
195	  `dot_bash_profile.tmpl` checks for `~/.profile` and sources it
196	  before `~/.bashrc` (with a `grep` guard against double-sourcing).
197	
198	When to use: only for **user-side** legacy compat. Our chezmoi-
199	managed configs DON'T live here.
200
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
# --- rclone ---
- name: Check if rclone is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.command: rclone version
  register: rclone_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Set rclone release architecture
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - rclone_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    rclone_release_arch: >-
      {{
        'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
        else 'arm-v7' if target_architecture == 'armv7l'
        else 'arm-v6' if target_architecture == 'armv6l'
        else ''
      }}

- name: Fail on unsupported architecture for rclone
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - rclone_check.rc != 0
    - rclone_release_arch == ''
  ansible.builtin.fail:
    msg: "Unsupported architecture for rclone official downloads: {{ target_architecture }}"
```

### 2. Full TOML for Reference Channels

#### `dot_config/television/cable/mlflow.toml`
```toml
[metadata]
name = "mlflow"
description = "MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models (file/sqlite/http backends)"
requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]

[source]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models",
]
display = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  ({split:\\t:4})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
no_sort = true

[preview]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full    | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view metrics | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
]
header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"

[ui]
input_header = "MLflow"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open-or-drill"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"
ctrl-b = "actions:open-browser"
alt-r = "actions:drill-runs"
alt-j = "actions:dump-json"

[actions.open-or-drill]
description = "Drill into experiment runs / open JSON detail"
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
  __hint__) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
  *[!0-9]*) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
  *) MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" ;;
esac"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-id]
description = "Copy row id to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.open-browser]
description = "Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only)"
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; uri="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"; case "$uri" in http://*|https://*) ;; *) printf '[open-browser] needs MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http(s)://…\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$id" in __hint__) printf '[open-browser] no row selected\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; url="$uri/"; if [ "${#id}" = "32" ] && printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/0/runs/$id"; elif printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/$id"; else url="$uri/#/models/$id"; fi; if command -v open >/dev/null; then open "$url"; elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null; then xdg-open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 & elif command -v wslview >/dev/null; then wslview "$url"; else printf '[open-browser] no opener\\n'; sleep 2; fi"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.drill-runs]
description = "Re-launch tv scoped to experiment"
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
  __hint__|*[!0-9]*) printf '[drill-runs] not an experiment row\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;;
esac
MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" """
mode = "execute"

[actions.dump-json]
description = "Print full JSON detail to terminal"
command = "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
```

**Key patterns here:**
- **Multiple sources** (Ctrl+S cycling): `command` is a list of shell commands
- **Preview cycling** (Ctrl+F): `command` is also a list (each cycle is a different preview)
- **Helper scripts** (`mlflow-source.py`, `mlflow-preview.py`): Deployed in `~/.config/television/`
- **Piping to colorizers**: `| bat --color=always --plain --paging=never` for JSON; `| jq -C` for JSON in other channels
- **Custom actions** with `mode = "execute"` for blocking operations, `mode = "fork"` for non-blocking
- **`no_sort = true`**: Preserve helper script's output order (important for cycling sources with semantics)
- **Clipboard abstraction**: Reusable `_clip()` function handles pbcopy/wl-copy/xclip/OSC 52

[metadata]

command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.status]
description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"
command = "fleet chezmoi status --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.info]
description = "fleet info for this host"
command = "fleet info --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.pueue]
description = "fleet pueue for this host"
command = "fleet pueue --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
```

**Key patterns here:**
- **Simple source command**: Single shell command (no cycling)
- **Preview delegates to CLI**: `fleet hosts --describe` — not a helper script
- **Alt+ namespace**: Avoids tmux/TV conflicts (convention across mac-apps, linux-apps, ssh-config)
- **Multiple Alt-actions**: Each invokes a different fleet subcommand
- **Consistent output format**: Tab-delimited with `{split:\t:N}` placeholders for action substitution

#### `dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl`
```toml
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
[metadata]
name = "mac-apps"
description = "macOS apps — graceful quit / restart / activate / hide via Apple Events"
requirements = []

[source]
command = """osascript -e 'tell application "System Events"' -e 'set out to ""' -e 'repeat with p in (every application process whose background only is false)' -e 'set out to out & (unix id of p) & tab & (name of p) & linefeed' -e 'end repeat' -e 'return out' -e 'end tell' 2>/dev/null"""
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:1}"

[preview]
command = [
  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'
ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command 2>/dev/null
echo
lsappinfo info "$pid" 2>/dev/null | head -30""",
  """name='{split:\\t:1}'
. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh 2>/dev/null
printf 'App: %s\\n' "$name"
if appresponsive "$name" 2>/dev/null; then
  printf 'Status: responsive\\n'
else
  printf 'Status: NOT responding\\n'
fi
printf '\\n(2s Apple Event timeout)\\n'""",
]
header = "{split:\\t:1}  (pid {split:\\t:0})"

[ui]
input_header = "macOS Apps"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:activate"
alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]
alt-r = ["actions:restart", "reload_source"]
alt-h = "actions:hide"
alt-k = ["actions:force-kill", "reload_source"]
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:probe"

[actions.activate]
description = "Bring app to front"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appactivate '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.quit]
description = "Graceful Quit (⌘Q-equivalent Apple Event)"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appquit '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.restart]
description = "Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && apprestart '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.hide]
description = "Hide app windows"
command = """osascript -e 'on run argv' -e 'tell application "System Events" to set visible of (first process whose name is (item 1 of argv)) to false' -e 'end run' -- '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.force-kill]
description = "SIGKILL by PID"
command = "kill -9 '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.info]
description = "Detail pager: ps + full lsappinfo"
command = """pid='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:1}'; { printf '=== %s (pid %s) ===\\n\\n' "$name" "$pid"; ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command; printf '\\n'; lsappinfo info "$pid"; } 2>/dev/null | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "Probe app responsiveness"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && name='{split:\\t:1}' && (appresponsive "$name" 5 && printf '%s: responsive\\n' "$name" || printf '%s: NOT responding\\n' "$name"); sleep 2"""
mode = "execute"
{{ end -}}
```

**Key patterns here:**
- **Chezmoi template** (`.tmpl`): Gated with `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}` so it only renders on macOS
- **Keybindings with multiple actions**: `alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]` chains an action with a TV built-in command
- **Source-helper function**: `. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh` sources a shell helper file that defines `appactivate`, `appquit`, `apprestart`, `appresponsive`
- **Inline Apple Events**: Direct `osascript` for one-off verbs (hide) to keep channel self-contained
