#### `dot_config/television/cable/linux-apps.toml.tmpl`
```toml
{{- if and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") -}}
[metadata]
name = "linux-apps"
description = "Linux apps — graceful quit / restart / activate via gtk-launch + pkill"
requirements = []

[source]
command = """sh -c '. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh 2>/dev/null && applist --pids' 2>/dev/null"""
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:1}"

[preview]
command = [
  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'
name='{split:\\t:1}'
ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,comm 2>/dev/null
echo
printf '=== child processes ===\\n'
pgrep -P "$pid" -af 2>/dev/null | head -10
echo
printf '=== full command line ===\\n'
tr '\\0' ' ' < "/proc/$pid/cmdline" 2>/dev/null | head -c 500
echo""",
  """name='{split:\\t:1}'
. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh 2>/dev/null
printf 'App: %s\\n' "$name"
if appresponsive "$name" 2>/dev/null; then
  printf 'Status: responsive\\n'
else
  printf 'Status: NOT responding (or hung / not running / no MPRIS handle)\\n'
fi""",
]
header = "{split:\\t:1}  (pid {split:\\t:0})"

[ui]
input_header = "Linux Apps"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:activate"
alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]
alt-r = ["actions:restart", "reload_source"]
alt-k = ["actions:force-kill", "reload_source"]
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:probe"

[actions.activate]
description = "Bring app to front"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh && appactivate '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.quit]
description = "Graceful Quit (SIGTERM via app's pkill pattern)"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh && appquit '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.restart]
description = "Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh && apprestart '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.force-kill]
description = "SIGKILL by PID"
command = "kill -9 '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "fork"

[actions.info]
description = "Detail pager: ps + pgrep tree + cmdline"
command = """pid='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:1}'; { printf '=== %s (pid %s) ===\\n\\n' "$name" "$pid"; ps -p "$pid" -o pid,ppid,user,etime,pcpu,pmem,rss,command 2>/dev/null; printf '\\n=== child processes ===\\n'; pgrep -P "$pid" -af 2>/dev/null; printf '\\n=== full command line ===\\n'; tr '\\0' ' ' < "/proc/$pid/cmdline" 2>/dev/null; printf '\\n'; } 2>/dev/null | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "Probe app responsiveness (MPRIS-only)"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh && name='{split:\\t:1}' && (appresponsive "$name" 5 && printf '%s: responsive\\n' "$name" || printf '%s: NOT responding\\n' "$name"); sleep 2"""
mode = "execute"
{{ end -}}
```

**Key patterns here:**
- **Cross-platform Alt-key mirroring**: Same keybindings (alt-q, alt-r, alt-k, etc.) as mac-apps, but different implementation
- **Template gating**: `{{- if and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") -}}` gates to Linux with profile check
- **Shared interface contract**: Same `appactivate`, `appquit`, `apprestart`, `appresponsive` function names (defined in `56_linux_apps.sh`), different innards

### 3. TOML Schema Fields Across All Channels

| Section | Field | Type | Purpose | Examples |
|---------|-------|------|---------|----------|
| `[metadata]` | `name` | string | Channel identifier (used in `tv <name>`) | `mlflow`, `fleet-hosts` |
| | `description` | string | One-liner shown in `tv channels` and help | `"MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models"` |
| | `requirements` | array | CLI tools this channel needs (informational) | `["mlflow", "uv"]`, `["fleet", "ssh"]` |
| `[source]` | `command` | string or array | Shell command(s) to generate rows; array = Ctrl+S cycling sources | `"fleet hosts --list-tsv"` or array of commands |
| | `display` | string | How to format row for display (uses `{split:\t:N}` placeholders) | `"{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"` |
| | `output` | string | What gets piped to actions (uses `{split:\t:N}` placeholders) | `"{split:\\t:0}"` (just the ID) |
| | `watch` | float | Auto-refresh interval in seconds; omit for manual-only | `2.0`, `5.0` |
| | `no_sort` | boolean | Preserve command's output order (important for semantic cycling) | `true` (mlflow, pueue) |
| `[preview]` | `command` | string or array | Shell command(s) to generate preview pane; array = Ctrl+F cycling | `"fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"` or array |
| | `header` | string | Title line for preview pane | `"{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:2})"` |
| `[ui]` | `input_header` | string | Picker title (top-left) | `"MLflow"`, `"Super Productivity"` |
| `[ui.preview_panel]` | `size` | integer | Preview pane width (chars) | `60` |
| `[keybindings]` | keys | string or array | Bind key to action name or chain with TV built-ins | `"enter = "actions:connect""` or `["actions:quit", "reload_source"]` |
| `[actions.NAME]` | `description` | string | Help text for the action | `"SSH into the selected fleet host"` |
| | `command` | string | Shell command to execute (uses `{split:\t:N}` for substitution) | `"ssh '{split:\\t:1}'"` |
| | `mode` | string | `"execute"` (blocking, user sees output) or `"fork"` (non-blocking) | `"execute"` for SSH, `"fork"` for quick commands |

**Placeholder syntax:**
- `{split:\t:N}` — Split row by tabs, extract column N (0-indexed)
- `{split: :N}` — Split row by spaces, extract column N
- Whitespace matters: `{split:\\t:0}` is escaped tab, `{split: :0}` is space

### 5. Schema Fields Actually Used Across Channels

**Always present:**
- `[metadata]` with `name`, `description`
- `[source]` with `command`, `display`, `output`
- `[keybindings]` with at least one binding (usually `enter`)
- `[actions.*]` sections with `command` and `mode`

**Optional but common:**
- `[preview]` — most channels have it (some omit to reduce overhead)
- `[ui]` with `input_header` — helps with branding
- `[ui.preview_panel]` with `size` — useful for wide previews (JSON, config)
- `watch` — auto-refresh (pueue: 2s, super-productivity: 5s; most channels omit)
- `requirements` — metadata only; TV doesn't enforce it
- `no_sort = true` — only when cycling sources have semantic meaning (mlflow, pueue)
- Multiple preview `command` entries for Ctrl+F cycling

**Action patterns:**
- `mode = "execute"` — for SSH, pager, long-running tasks (user sees output)
- `mode = "fork"` — for quick side-effects (copy, kill -TERM, activate window)
- Keybindings can chain: `["actions:verb", "reload_source"]` to refresh after mutation

### 6. Helper Scripts and Backing Tools

**Python helpers** (in `~/.config/television/`):
- `mlflow-source.py` — Parses MLflow tracking backends (file, sqlite, http); implements source cycling
- `mlflow-preview.py` — Renders experiment/run/model JSON with `--view` (full, metrics)
- `super-productivity-source.sh` — Queries local REST API (http://127.0.0.1:3876)
- `agent-sessions.py` — Lists Claude Code agent panes

**Shell helpers** (in `~/.config/shell/`):
- `54_macos_apps.sh` — Defines `appactivate`, `appquit`, `apprestart`, `appresponsive` (Apple Events)
- `56_linux_apps.sh` — Defines same functions via gtk-launch, pkill patterns, MPRIS
- These are sourced by actions to keep channel TOML DRY

**CLI tools that channels shell out to:**
- `fleet` (custom umbrella CLI) — `fleet hosts --list-tsv`, `fleet hosts --describe`, `fleet chezmoi status`, etc.
- `lsof` / `ss` — Port listener enumeration (ports.toml)
- `pueue` — Task queue CLI (pueue.toml sources `pueue status --json`)
- `curl` + `jq` — Super Productivity REST API client
- `osascript` — Direct Apple Events (mac-apps inline, no helper needed)

### Recommendations for `dot_config/television/cable/rclone.toml`

Based on the patterns above, here's what a consistent rclone channel should look like:

**Likely structure:**
```toml
[metadata]
name = "rclone"
description = "rclone remotes: list, browse mounts, show stats"
requirements = ["rclone"]

[source]
command = [
  "rclone listremotes",           # Source 1: all remotes
  "rclone config dumpsecure",     # Source 2: config detail (JSON)
]
display = "{split: :0}"           # or parse JSON if using dumpsecure
output = "{split: :0}"

[preview]
command = "rclone about '{split: :0}' --json | jq -C . || rclone config show '{split: :0}'"

[ui]
input_header = "rclone Remotes"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:copy_remote"
alt-s = "actions:size_stats"      # rclone size (storage quota)
alt-b = "actions:browse"          # rclone lsf for listing
alt-m = "actions:mount_info"      # rclone mount status (if running)

[actions.copy_remote]
description = "Copy remote name to clipboard"
command = "_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z \"$d\" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' \"$d\" | pbcopy; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | _clip"
mode = "fork"

[actions.size_stats]
description = "Show remote size and quota"
command = "rclone about '{split: :0}' --json | jq -C . | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
```

**Key considerations:**
- Rclone has no native "drill-in" equivalent, so Ctrl+S cycling is less critical (maybe list remotes vs. config)
- Alt+S for size stats mirrors the `ssh-config` / `fleet-hosts` Alt-key convention
- Use `rclone --json` to output JSON, pipe to `jq -C` for color (like super-productivity)
- Helper script may not be needed (unlike mlflow, fleet); rclone CLI is self-contained
- Consider `watch = 0` (manual refresh only) — rclone remotes don't change frequently

## 1. **tools.toml parsing & schema**

The channel uses a single-pass `awk` parser:
```awk
awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
  inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
  desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
  printf "%-22s  %s\\n", inv, desc
}' ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md
```

**Row format** (from cli-tools.md):
```markdown
| Command | Invocation | Description | Notes |
|---------|------------|-------------|-------|
| `rclone` | `rclone ` | Sync files to/from cloud storage | `rclone sync src dst` |
```

Extracts columns 3 (backtick-wrapped invocation) and 4 (description). The **trailing space in invocation** (e.g. `rclone `) signals "needs argument before run."

**Preview pane** tries `tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en $tool` first, falls back to `$tool --help | head -50`. No special rclone config exists.

The `rclone help` canonical format lists ~45 subcommands (about, archive, authorize, backend, bisync ... mount, move ...) in standard `Available commands:` block. Easy to parse or curate from.

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should the channel mix remotes vs. subcommand reference? The mlflow channel uses Ctrl+S to cycle source lists within a single channel — same pattern here vs. separate channels?**

Options:
- **One channel, cycling sources** - `tv rclone` opens with remotes by default; Ctrl+S cycles to subcommand list. Matches mlflow's pattern. Single entry point.
- **Two channels** - `tv rclone` for remotes only, `tv rclone-help` for subcommand reference. Each does one thing well, simpler TOML per file.
- **Remotes only (drop subcommand ref)** - Subcommands are already discoverable via `tv tools` → rclone → tldr/--help. Skip duplication. Just build the remote browser.

**Default preview depth for a selected remote — how aggressive should the directory listing be?**

Options:
- **Top-level only, deeper on Ctrl+F** - Default preview shows `rclone about` + top-level dirs (fast, ~1s). Ctrl+F cycles to a deeper view (`--max-depth 2`) for users who want it. Recommended.
- **Always show 2 layers** - Preview always runs `rclone lsd --max-depth 2`. Richer but can be slow on cold/large remotes (S3 list-objects, gdrive API).
- **Just `rclone about`, no listing** - Preview shows only the quota/usage JSON. Directory browsing is a separate action (Alt+B) that opens a drill-in picker.

**Should the preview include `rclone config show <remote>` (revealing access keys / obscured tokens)?**

Options:
- **No — separate action only** - Default previews skip config. Alt+C runs `rclone config show` in a pager so the user opts in explicitly. Avoids accidental over-shoulder leaks.
- **Yes — cycle to it via Ctrl+F** - Include `rclone config show` as one of the cycling preview views. Convenient but secrets-adjacent strings (obscured passwords) flash in the preview pane.
- **No config view at all** - Don't include config browsing anywhere. Users who want it can `rclone config show` themselves.

**For drill-in (browsing into a remote's directories), what behavior should Enter trigger?**

Options:
- **Re-launch tv scoped to that remote** - Enter on `remote:` spawns `tv rclone` with source rewritten to `rclone lsf -d remote:` (immediate children); pressing Enter on a child drills deeper. Matches mlflow's MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID drill pattern.
- **Open `rclone ncdu` for that remote** - Enter launches `rclone ncdu remote:` (rclone's built-in TUI disk usage browser). Best UX for large trees but pulls user out of tv into a full-screen TUI.
- **Copy `remote:` to clipboard** - Enter just copies the remote name to clipboard so the user can paste it into a shell command. Simple, no surprises.


**Answer:** Two channels, Top-level only, deeper on Ctrl+F, Yes — cycle to it via Ctrl+F, Re-launch tv scoped to that remote
</details></tool-use>

```md
# rclone Television channels — remotes browser + subcommand reference

## Context

`rclone` is installed by `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (Homebrew on macOS, `downloads.rclone.org` standalone on Linux) and listed in `dot_config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md`, but it has no dedicated tv channel yet. Users who run `tv tools` and pick `rclone` get only the 8-example tldr page that the question quoted.

The ask is a tv-native surface for rclone that:

- **Previews remotes** — quota / about + top-level dirs at a glance, with deeper drill-ins on demand.
- **Surfaces about/summary info** — `rclone about --json`, `rclone size --json`, `rclone config show` so users don't have to remember which subcommand answers which question.
- **Quick-references subcommands** — discover the ~45 commands in `rclone help` and read their `--help` without leaving tv.

Per the clarifying questions: **two separate channels** (one per concern), preview defaults to top-level only with **Ctrl+F cycling** to deeper views including `rclone config show`, and **Enter on a remote drills in** by re-launching tv scoped to that remote (mlflow's drill pattern).

## Files to create

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `dot_config/television/cable/rclone.toml` | Remotes browser — drill-in picker, about/size/config previews, multi-action Alt-key bindings |
| `dot_config/television/cable/rclone-help.toml` | Subcommand reference — parses `rclone help`, previews `rclone <sub> --help` |

No helper scripts. Both channels stay self-contained in TOML — `rclone` ships rich JSON output (`--json`) and structured help, so the preview commands are short one-liners that pipe to `jq -C` / `bat`. This matches the `fleet-hosts.toml` style (shell-out to the CLI) rather than the `mlflow.toml` style (Python helpers in `~/.config/television/`).

## `rclone.toml` design

**Source** (initial): `rclone listremotes` → one `remote:` per line.

**Source rewriting on drill** (Enter action): `tv rclone --source-command "..."` with a command that calls `rclone lsf -d PATH` and prefixes each row with the parent path so subsequent drills keep working. The `--input-header` is updated to show the current path crumb.

**Display / output**: rows are just the full path (`remote:` or `remote:dir1/dir2/`). Single-column TSV-free format keeps drill-in easy.

**Preview cycling (Ctrl+F)** — four views in order, with path-aware branching so a drilled subdir doesn't try to call `rclone about` (which is per-remote, not per-path):

1. **Default — about + top-level dirs**. If path is a remote root (`remote:`), runs `rclone about --json | jq -C .` then `rclone lsd remote: --max-depth 1`. If path is a subdir, runs `rclone lsd PATH --max-depth 1` then `rclone size PATH --json | jq -C .`.
2. **Deeper listing** — `rclone lsd PATH --max-depth 2` (slower; opt-in via Ctrl+F).
3. **File-level listing** — `rclone lsf PATH | head -200` (shows both files and dirs flat; useful for "what's actually in here").
4. **Config view** — `rclone config show REMOTE` (extracted from path with `awk -F: '{print $1}'`). Header notes that obscured tokens are reversible base64, not encryption.

**Keybindings** — follows the `fleet-hosts.toml` + `mac-apps.toml.tmpl` Alt-key convention (Alt+ avoids tmux/TV conflicts; CLAUDE.md "Keybinding" cross-file rule):

| Key | Action | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Enter | drill-in | re-launch tv scoped to selected path |
| Ctrl+Y | copy path | uses the same `_clip()` abstraction (pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC 52) lifted from `mlflow.toml` |
| Alt+A | about (paged) | `rclone about PATH --json | jq -C . | less -R` |
| Alt+S | size (paged) | `rclone size PATH --json | jq -C . | less -R` — counts objects + total bytes |
| Alt+B | browse with ncdu | `rclone ncdu PATH` — opt-in full-screen TUI for users who explicitly want it |
| Alt+C | config show (paged) | `rclone config show REMOTE | less -R` — the explicit opt-in for config viewing |
| Alt+M | mount status | `mount | grep rclone || echo '[no active rclone mounts]'` |

## `rclone-help.toml` design

**Source**: parse `rclone help` for the `Available commands:` block. One-liner:

\```sh
rclone help 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Available [Cc]ommands:/{f=1; next} /^Flags:/{f=0} f && /^[[:space:]]+[a-z]/ {sub(/^[[:space:]]+/,""); print}'
\```

Each row becomes `<subcmd>  <description>`. Display extracts column 0 with `{split: :0}` (matches `tools.toml` placeholder style).

**Preview cycling (Ctrl+F)**:

1. `rclone <sub> --help | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=help` — primary view.
2. `tldr rclone-<sub> 2>/dev/null || echo '[no tldr page]'` — fallback to upstream tldr if it exists (most don't, but `rclone-copy`, `rclone-sync`, `rclone-mount` do).

**Keybindings**:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter | full `--help` in `less -R` so the user can scroll |
| Ctrl+Y | copy `rclone <sub> ` (trailing space, mirrors the `cli-tools.md` "needs argument" convention) |

## Critical files referenced

- `dot_config/television/cable/mlflow.toml` — copy the `_clip()` action body and the `--source-command` drill-in pattern verbatim
- `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` — shell-out-to-CLI style for the simpler subcommand channel
- `dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl` — Alt-key namespacing convention + `reload_source` chaining
- `dot_config/television/cable/tools.toml` — awk parsing pattern for the subcommand source

## Cross-file maintenance (per CLAUDE.md table)

- **No `mkdocs.yml` change** — no new doc page is being added.
- **No `cli-tools.md` change** — rclone is already listed.
- **No alias-table change** — these are tv channels, not shell aliases.
- **No completions to add** — rclone's own `complete` machinery is already handled by `generate_completions.sh` (it ships `rclone completion zsh` / `rclone completion bash`); auditing this is **not** in scope for this plan but worth a follow-up if missing.

## Verification

1. **Render the channels** — `chezmoi diff dot_config/television/cable/rclone.toml dot_config/television/cable/rclone-help.toml`, then `chezmoi apply` (no run-scripts triggered since only static files change).
2. **Confirm tv discovers them** — `tv channels` should list `rclone` and `rclone-help` with the metadata descriptions.
3. **Functional smoke (remotes)**:
   - `tv rclone` → picker opens; if no remotes are configured, the source returns empty (acceptable; matches `fleet-hosts` behavior on a fresh host).
   - Configure a throwaway local remote: `rclone config create _tvtest local type=local` → `tv rclone` lists `_tvtest:`.
   - Cycle preview (Ctrl+F) through all 4 views; confirm Ctrl+F #4 shows `rclone config show _tvtest`.
   - Enter → drills in; input-header updates to `rclone / _tvtest:`; preview switches to subdir mode (no `about`).
   - Alt+A / Alt+S / Alt+C exit to pager and return to picker cleanly.
   - Cleanup: `rclone config delete _tvtest`.
4. **Functional smoke (help)**:
   - `tv rclone-help` lists ~45 subcommands.
   - Pick `mount`; default preview shows `rclone mount --help`; Ctrl+F cycles to `tldr rclone-mount`.
   - Enter pages `rclone mount --help` in `less -R`.
   - Ctrl+Y copies `rclone mount ` (with trailing space) to clipboard.
5. **Cross-platform** — both channels are plain `.toml` (no `.tmpl`), so they deploy identically on macOS and Linux. Smoke-test the Alt+M mount-status action on Linux too (`mount` grep syntax is portable).

| Alt+S | size (paged) | `rclone size PATH --json | jq -C . | less -R` — counts objects + total bytes |
| Alt+B | browse with ncdu | `rclone ncdu PATH` — opt-in full-screen TUI for users who explicitly want it |
| Alt+C | config show (paged) | `rclone config show REMOTE | less -R` — the explicit opt-in for config viewing |
| Alt+M | mount status | `mount | grep rclone || echo '[no active rclone mounts]'` |

## `rclone-help.toml` design

**Source**: parse `rclone help` for the `Available commands:` block. One-liner:

```sh
rclone help 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Available [Cc]ommands:/{f=1; next} /^Flags:/{f=0} f && /^[[:space:]]+[a-z]/ {sub(/^[[:space:]]+/,""); print}'
```

Each row becomes `<subcmd>  <description>`. Display extracts column 0 with `{split: :0}` (matches `tools.toml` placeholder style).

**Preview cycling (Ctrl+F)**:

1. `rclone <sub> --help | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=help` — primary view.
2. `tldr rclone-<sub> 2>/dev/null || echo '[no tldr page]'` — fallback to upstream tldr if it exists (most don't, but `rclone-copy`, `rclone-sync`, `rclone-mount` do).

**Keybindings**:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter | full `--help` in `less -R` so the user can scroll |
| Ctrl+Y | copy `rclone <sub> ` (trailing space, mirrors the `cli-tools.md` "needs argument" convention) |

## Critical files referenced

- `dot_config/television/cable/mlflow.toml` — copy the `_clip()` action body and the `--source-command` drill-in pattern verbatim
- `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` — shell-out-to-CLI style for the simpler subcommand channel
- `dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl` — Alt-key namespacing convention + `reload_source` chaining
- `dot_config/television/cable/tools.toml` — awk parsing pattern for the subcommand source

## Cross-file maintenance (per CLAUDE.md table)

- **No `mkdocs.yml` change** — no new doc page is being added.
- **No `cli-tools.md` change** — rclone is already listed.
- **No alias-table change** — these are tv channels, not shell aliases.
- **No completions to add** — rclone's own `complete` machinery is already handled by `generate_completions.sh` (it ships `rclone completion zsh` / `rclone completion bash`); auditing this is **not** in scope for this plan but worth a follow-up if missing.

## Verification

1. **Render the channels** — `chezmoi diff dot_config/television/cable/rclone.toml dot_config/television/cable/rclone-help.toml`, then `chezmoi apply` (no run-scripts triggered since only static files change).
2. **Confirm tv discovers them** — `tv channels` should list `rclone` and `rclone-help` with the metadata descriptions.
3. **Functional smoke (remotes)**:
   - `tv rclone` → picker opens; if no remotes are configured, the source returns empty (acceptable; matches `fleet-hosts` behavior on a fresh host).
   - Configure a throwaway local remote: `rclone config create _tvtest local type=local` → `tv rclone` lists `_tvtest:`.
   - Cycle preview (Ctrl+F) through all 4 views; confirm Ctrl+F #4 shows `rclone config show _tvtest`.
   - Enter → drills in; input-header updates to `rclone / _tvtest:`; preview switches to subdir mode (no `about`).
   - Alt+A / Alt+S / Alt+C exit to pager and return to picker cleanly.
   - Cleanup: `rclone config delete _tvtest`.
4. **Functional smoke (help)**:
   - `tv rclone-help` lists ~45 subcommands.
   - Pick `mount`; default preview shows `rclone mount --help`; Ctrl+F cycles to `tldr rclone-mount`.
   - Enter pages `rclone mount --help` in `less -R`.
   - Ctrl+Y copies `rclone mount ` (with trailing space) to clipboard.
5. **Cross-platform** — both channels are plain `.toml` (no `.tmpl`), so they deploy identically on macOS and Linux. Smoke-test the Alt+M mount-status action on Linux too (`mount` grep syntax is portable).

```text
1	# MLflow channel for television (tv).
2	# Browse experiments, runs, and registered models against any MLflow tracking
3	# backend (file:./mlruns, sqlite:///path/to/mlflow.db, or http://server:port).
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   tv mlflow
7	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow
8	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
9	#
10	# Prerequisites:
11	#   - `mlflow` installed (provided by dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools — the
12	#     CLI binary is what we exec under the `uv run --script` shebang of the
13	#     two helpers).
14	#   - `uv` on PATH (installed by uv role; required to resolve the PEP 723
15	#     inline-deps block in mlflow-source.py / mlflow-preview.py).
16	#
17	# Backend mode is resolved entirely from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI. When unset,
18	# mlflow 3.12+ auto-detects from $PWD: an `mlflow.db` file picks sqlite, an
19	# `mlruns/` dir picks file mode, otherwise it creates `mlruns/`. To pin a
20	# backend at launch time:
21	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://host:port tv mlflow
22	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
23	#
24	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
25	#   1. Experiments     all active experiments
26	#   2. Recent runs     top 50 runs across all experiments, by start_time desc
27	#   3. Runs (scoped)   runs in $MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID (hint row when unset;
28	#                      Alt+R on an experiment row sets it and re-launches tv)
29	#   4. Models          registered models from the model registry
30	#
31	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
32	#   1. Full JSON       params, metrics, tags, artifact_uri, timestamps
33	#   2. Metrics-only    sorted key=value table; or aggregated across recent
34	#                      runs for an experiment row
35	#
36	# Keybindings:
37	#   Enter      Context-aware:
38	#                experiment row -> re-launch tv scoped to that experiment's
39	#                                  runs (nested drill-in; Esc exits the
40	#                                  drilled view back to the shell)
41	#                run / model row -> open full JSON detail in pager
42	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard
43	#   Ctrl+O     Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only; prints a hint
44	#              otherwise)
45	#   Ctrl+B     Same as Ctrl+O — "B for browser" muscle-memory alias
46	#   Alt+R      Explicit drill — same as Enter on an experiment row,
47	#              available as a backup binding for muscle memory
48	#   Alt+J      Dump full JSON to terminal (paged)
49	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview
50	#   Ctrl+S     Cycle source
51	#
52	# No `watch` field: mlflow imports are heavy (~1s warm, several seconds cold);
53	# experiments and runs change on the minute scale anyway. Press Ctrl+R to
54	# refresh manually after logging a new run.
55	#
56	# Hint row sentinel: when the backend is unreachable or a source is unscoped,
57	# the helper emits a single row with id `__hint__`. Real mlflow ids never
58	# collide (experiment_ids are non-negative ints; run_ids are 32-hex; model
59	# names cannot contain `__hint__` in practice).
60	
61	[metadata]
62	name = "mlflow"
63	description = "MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models (file/sqlite/http backends)"
64	requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]
65	
66	[source]
67	command = [
68	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments",
69	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent",
70	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment",
71	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models",
72	]
73	display = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  ({split:\\t:4})"
74	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
75	no_sort = true
76	
77	[preview]
78	# Helper always emits valid JSON now; pipe through `bat -l json` so the
79	# preview pane gets syntax highlighting (numbers, strings, keys). Same
80	# trick super-productivity.toml plays with `jq -C`, but bat's truecolor
81	# theme is easier on the eyes for nested objects.
82	#
83	# `--paging=never` is load-bearing: bat detects "not a TTY" inside TV's
84	# preview pipe and would otherwise still buffer; we want streamed output.
85	# `--plain` strips line numbers / decorations so the preview pane shows
86	# only the rendered content.
87	command = [
88	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full    | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
89	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view metrics | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
90	]
91	header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"
92	
93	[ui]
94	input_header = "MLflow"
95	
96	[ui.preview_panel]
97	size = 60
98	
99	[keybindings]
100	enter = "actions:open-or-drill"
101	# Override TV's default ctrl-y (which copies the entire display row) with
102	# id-only copy. Matches super-productivity.toml's convention.
103	ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
104	ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"
105	# Ctrl+B is the muscle-memory alias — same action body as Ctrl+O. Reusing
106	# the existing action keeps the channel self-contained even if `mlf` (the
107	# umbrella CLI in dot_dotfiles/bin/) isn't installed.
108	ctrl-b = "actions:open-browser"
109	alt-r = "actions:drill-runs"
110	alt-j = "actions:dump-json"
111	
112	[actions.open-or-drill]
113	description = "Drill into experiment runs (experiment row) / open JSON detail (others)"
114	# Kind detection mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
115	#   __hint__       -> show the help JSON (helpful when MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is
116	#                     misconfigured: lets the user read the example URIs)
117	#   digit-only id  -> drill: re-exec tv with MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID + a
118	#                     --source-command override so the nested view shows ONLY
119	#                     this experiment's runs. Esc exits the drill back to
120	#                     the shell (TV does not have a back-stack; rerun
121	#                     `tv mlflow` for cross-experiment views).
122	#   anything else  -> open JSON detail in pager
123	#
124	# The header is set to "MLflow / <exp_name>" inside the drilled view so it's
125	# obvious you're in the nested context, not the top-level one. {split:\t:3}
126	# carries the experiment name in the experiments source layout (cols are:
127	# id, marker, lifecycle, name, last_update).
128	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
129	  __hint__) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
130	  *[!0-9]*) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
131	  *) MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" ;;
132	esac"""
133	mode = "execute"
134	
135	[actions.copy-id]
136	description = "Copy row id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard"
137	command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
138	mode = "fork"
139	
140	[actions.open-browser]
141	description = "Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only)"
142	# Build the URL inside the action so we read the live env var rather than
143	# baking it in. Inference mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
144	#   32-hex id -> need a roundtrip to find experiment_id, just open root
145	#   all-digit -> /#/experiments/<id>
146	#   else      -> /#/models/<name>
147	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; uri="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"; case "$uri" in http://*|https://*) ;; *) printf '[open-browser] needs MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http(s)://… — current: %s\\n' "${uri:-(unset)}"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$id" in __hint__) printf '[open-browser] no row selected\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; url="$uri/"; if [ "${#id}" = "32" ] && printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/0/runs/$id"; elif printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/$id"; else url="$uri/#/models/$id"; fi; if command -v open >/dev/null; then open "$url"; elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null; then xdg-open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 & elif command -v wslview >/dev/null; then wslview "$url"; else printf '[open-browser] no opener (open/xdg-open/wslview) — URL was: %s\\n' "$url"; sleep 2; fi"""
148	mode = "fork"
149	
150	[actions.drill-runs]
151	description = "Re-launch tv scoped to the highlighted experiment (Alt+R)"
152	# Same payload as the Enter drill branch — explicit binding for muscle
153	# memory and discoverability. No-op + hint on non-experiment rows so the
154	# user doesn't accidentally drill into an empty unscoped view.
155	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
156	  __hint__|*[!0-9]*) printf '[drill-runs] not an experiment row (id=%s). Move to the Experiments source (Ctrl+S) and try again.\\n' "$id"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;;
157	esac
158	MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" """
159	mode = "execute"
160	
161	[actions.dump-json]
162	description = "Print full JSON detail to terminal, paged"
163	command = "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"

1	# Custom fleet-hosts channel for television (tv).
2	# Sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — the same inventory used by
3	# `fleet chezmoi apply` / `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` /
4	# `fleet exec`. Mirrors the `ssh-config` cable's UX but reads fleet's TOML
5	# inventory instead of ~/.ssh/config, so hosts with explicit
6	# hostname/user/port/identity_file (no ssh_alias) are reachable too.
7	#
8	# The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to:
9	#   fleet hosts --list-tsv      (source — `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` lines)
10	#   fleet hosts --describe N    (preview pane content)
11	#   fleet hosts N               (Enter action — os.execvp("ssh", ...))
12	# So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes
13	# automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync).
14	#
15	# Usage:
16	#   tv fleet-hosts
17	#   fleet hosts          # same picker via the fleet umbrella
18	#   fleet hosts lab-box  # skip the picker, SSH directly
19	#
20	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
21	#   Enter      SSH into the selected host
22	#   Alt+T      BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login actually work?)
23	#   Alt+S      fleet chezmoi status scoped to this host
24	#   Alt+I      fleet info scoped to this host
25	#   Alt+P      fleet pueue scoped to this host
26	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
27	#
28	# `local = true` hosts are intentionally hidden — they live on the
29	# orchestrator and have no SSH endpoint. Run `fleet hosts --list-tsv
30	# --include-local` to confirm one is in the inventory.
31	
32	[metadata]
33	name = "fleet-hosts"
34	description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
35	requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]
36	
37	[source]
38	command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
39	# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
40	# e.g.   lab-box <TAB> lab-box <TAB> alias:lab-box
41	#        vps-tokyo <TAB> 203.0.113.42 <TAB> explicit:dwlee@203.0.113.42
42	display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
43	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
44	
45	[preview]
46	command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"
47	
48	[keybindings]
49	enter = "actions:connect"
50	alt-t = "actions:probe"
51	alt-s = "actions:status"
52	alt-i = "actions:info"
53	alt-p = "actions:pueue"
54	
55	[actions.connect]
56	description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
57	command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
58	mode = "execute"
59	
60	[actions.probe]
61	description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
62	command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
63	mode = "execute"
64	
65	[actions.status]
66	description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"
67	command = "fleet chezmoi status --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
68	mode = "execute"
69	
70	[actions.info]
71	description = "fleet info for this host"
72	command = "fleet info --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
73	mode = "execute"
74	
75	[actions.pueue]
76	description = "fleet pueue for this host"
77	command = "fleet pueue --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
78	mode = "execute"

1	# Custom tools cable channel for television (tv)
2	# Parses ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md at runtime — single source of truth.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   tv tools                               (from shell)
6	#   prefix + U in tmux                     (popup)
7	#   Alt+T in zsh                           (opens fzf ZLE variant instead)
8	#
9	# Keybindings:
10	#   Enter      Execute selected tool immediately
11	#   Ctrl+T     Show tldrf page (multi-language fallback) in terminal
12	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
13	#
14	# Preview shows tldr page (zh_TW → zh → en fallback) or --help output.
15	
16	[metadata]
17	name = "tools"
18	description = "CLI tools quick-launch: select a tool to execute it"
19	requirements = ["awk"]
20	
21	[source]
22	command = """
23	awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
24	  inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
25	  desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
26	  printf "%-22s  %s\\n", inv, desc
27	}' ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md
28	"""
29	
30	[preview]
31	command = """
32	tool=$(printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | sed 's/ *$//')
33	if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
34	  tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en "$tool" 2>/dev/null || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
35	else
36	  "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
37	fi
38	"""
39	
40	[keybindings]
41	enter = "actions:exec"
42	ctrl-t = "actions:tldrf"
43	
44	[actions.exec]
45	description = "Execute selected tool"
46	command = "{split: :0}"
47	mode = "execute"
48	
49	[actions.tldrf]
50	description = "Show tldr page (multi-language fallback)"
51	command = "zsh -ic 'tldrf {split: :0}'"
52	mode = "execute"
53
```

1	# Custom aliases cable channel for television (tv)
2	# Lists all runtime shell aliases and functions.
3	#
4	# Data source: ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt (generated by 12_television.zsh on
5	# shell startup). This avoids spawning `zsh -ic` which causes tty conflicts.
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   tv aliases                             (from shell)
9	#   Alt+A                                  (ZLE widget)
10	#
11	# Keybindings:
12	#   Enter      Execute selected alias/function
13	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy alias/function name to clipboard
14	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
15	#
16	# Preview shows full definition via `type`.
17	
18	[metadata]
19	name = "aliases"
20	description = "Shell aliases & functions: fuzzy search all shortcuts"
21	
22	[source]
23	command = "cat ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 'Cache not found. Open a new shell to generate it.'"
24	
25	[preview]
26	command = """
27	name='{split: :0}'
28	kind='{split: :1}'
29	if [ "$kind" = "alias" ]; then
30	  grep "^$name[[:space:]]" ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt 2>/dev/null
31	else
32	  zsh --no-rcs -c "autoload -Uz $name 2>/dev/null; whence -f $name 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null || echo "$name (function)"
33	fi
34	"""
35	
36	[keybindings]
37	enter = "actions:exec"
38	ctrl-y = "actions:copy"
39	
40	[actions.exec]
41	description = "Execute selected alias/function"
42	command = "{split: :0}"
43	mode = "execute"
44	
45	[actions.copy]
46	description = "Copy name to clipboard"
47	command = """
48	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
49	  printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | pbcopy
50	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
51	  printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | wl-copy
52	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	  printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | xclip -selection clipboard
54	fi
55	"""
56	mode = "fork"

1	# Clash / mihomo config channel for television (tv).
2	# Fuzzy-search proxies, proxy-groups, rules and runtime controller info from a
3	# local Clash or mihomo config YAML. `tv clash` is the YAML-backed picker: it
4	# prefers the active Clash profile from ~/.config/clash/profiles/list.yml when
5	# present, then falls back to legacy config.{yaml,yml} paths. Controller-backed
6	# browsing lives in the separate `tv clash-api` channel.
7	#
8	# Usage:
9	#   tv clash
10	#
11	# Config discovery (first match wins):
12	#   $CLASH_CONFIG                                 (explicit override)
13	#   ~/.config/clash/profiles/list.yml -> active profiles/<time>.yml
14	#   ~/.config/clash/config.{yaml,yml}
15	#   ~/.config/mihomo/config.{yaml,yml}
16	#   ~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.{yaml,yml}
17	#   ~/Library/Application Support/mihomo/config.{yaml,yml}
18	#
19	# Prereqs: `uv` (bootstrap) + `curl` (base ansible role). `bat` and `jq` are
20	# used when present for nicer previews; PyYAML is auto-fetched by uv on first
21	# run. External-controller API is optional — when absent, all browse and
22	# latency-via-nc+ping flows still work, only the mutating Alt-key actions
23	# gracefully no-op.
24	#
25	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
26	#   1. Proxies              one row per proxies[] entry
27	#   2. Proxy Groups         one row per proxy-groups[] entry
28	#   3. Rules                one row per rules[] entry (indexed #NNNN)
29	#   4. Summary              top-level scalars (port, mode, external-controller)
30	#   5. API                  live controller health + traffic / connection stats
31	#                         (still uses the runtime controller, not the profile's
32	#                         stale external-controller field)
33	#
34	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
35	#   1. Main      selected entry's YAML block (bat -l yaml when available)
36	#   2. Latency   Clash API /proxies/:name/delay; falls back to nc -z + ping
37	#   3. Meta      groups referencing a proxy / full group YAML / sibling rules
38	#
39	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts):
40	#   Enter      Show full YAML of selected entry (execute mode)
41	#              On the synthetic `none` row: opens $EDITOR on a new config.
42	#   Alt+T      Latency test (API /proxies/:name/delay OR direct TCP probe)
43	#   Alt+S      Switch a proxy-group to this proxy (requires a group picked
44	#              via fzf, uses PUT /proxies/:group) — proxy rows only
45	#   Alt+C      Close all connections (DELETE /connections) with y/N confirm
46	#   Alt+R      Reload config (PUT /configs?force=true, uses on-disk path)
47	#   Alt+D      Open external-ui or a hosted dashboard in the browser
48	#   Alt+E      Edit the resolved config file in $EDITOR
49	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy the proxy's server:port (proxy rows) / name otherwise
50	#   Alt+Y      Copy the row's name field to clipboard
51	#
52	# Row schema (TSV): kind \t name \t type_or_meta \t server_or_target \t extra
53	#   kind ∈ {proxy, group, rule, config, api, none}
54	# Actions switch on kind so wrong-kind keys become 1-second toasts.
55	
56	[metadata]
57	name = "clash"
58	description = "Clash/mihomo config: proxies, groups, rules, latency tests, controller API"
59	requirements = ["curl", "uv"]
60	
61	[source]
62	command = [
63	  "$HOME/.config/television/clash-source.sh proxies",
64	  "$HOME/.config/television/clash-source.sh groups",
65	  "$HOME/.config/television/clash-source.sh rules",
66	  "$HOME/.config/television/clash-source.sh summary",
67	  "$HOME/.config/television/clash-source.sh api",
68	]
69	display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  [{split:\\t:2}]  {split:\\t:3}  {split:\\t:4}"
70	output = "{split:\\t:0}\t{split:\\t:1}"
71	no_sort = true
72	
73	[preview]
74	command = [
75	  "$HOME/.config/television/clash-preview.sh main    '{split:\\t:0}' '{split:\\t:1}'",
76	  "$HOME/.config/television/clash-preview.sh latency '{split:\\t:0}' '{split:\\t:1}'",
77	  "$HOME/.config/television/clash-preview.sh meta    '{split:\\t:0}' '{split:\\t:1}'",
78	]
79	header = "{split:\\t:0}: {split:\\t:1}"
80	
81	[ui]
82	input_header = "Clash"
83	
84	[ui.preview_panel]
85	size = 55
86	
87	[keybindings]
88	enter = "actions:show"
89	alt-t = "actions:test_latency"
90	alt-s = "actions:switch_proxy"
91	alt-c = ["actions:close_connections", "reload_source"]
92	alt-r = ["actions:reload_config", "reload_source"]
93	alt-d = "actions:open_dashboard"
94	alt-e = "actions:edit_config"
95	# Override TV global ctrl-y (copies full display line) to copy the server
96	# address for proxies, or the name otherwise.
97	ctrl-y = "actions:copy_server"
98	alt-y = "actions:copy_name"
99	
100	[actions.show]
101	description = "Show full YAML of the selected entry"
102	command = """
103	kind='{split:\\t:0}'
104	name='{split:\\t:1}'
105	case "$kind" in
106	  none)
107	    cfg="$HOME/.config/clash/config.yaml"
108	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$cfg")"
109	    if [ ! -f "$cfg" ]; then
110	      printf 'port: 7890\\nsocks-port: 7891\\nexternal-controller: 127.0.0.1:9090\\nmode: Rule\\nproxies: []\\nproxy-groups: []\\nrules:\\n  - MATCH,DIRECT\\n' > "$cfg"
111	    fi
112	    "${EDITOR:-vi}" "$cfg"
113	    ;;
114	  *)
115	    "$HOME/.config/television/clash-preview.sh" main "$kind" "$name"
116	    echo
117	    echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
118	    read -r _
119	    ;;
120	esac
121	"""
122	mode = "execute"
123	
124	[actions.test_latency]
125	description = "Test proxy latency (Clash API /delay or direct TCP probe)"
126	command = """
127	kind='{split:\\t:0}'
128	if [ "$kind" != "proxy" ] && [ "$kind" != "group" ]; then
129	  printf 'Alt+T only applies to proxies/groups (got kind=%s)\\n' "$kind"
130	  sleep 1
131	  exit 0
132	fi
133	"$HOME/.config/television/clash-preview.sh" latency '{split:\\t:0}' '{split:\\t:1}'
134	echo
135	echo '[Press Enter to exit]'
136	read -r _
137	"""
138	mode = "execute"
139	
140	[actions.switch_proxy]
141	description = "Switch a proxy-group's selection to the highlighted proxy"
142	command = "$HOME/.config/television/clash-switch.sh yaml '{split:\\t:0}' '{split:\\t:1}'"
143	mode = "execute"
144	
145	[actions.close_connections]
146	description = "Close all active connections (DELETE /connections)"
147	command = """
148	{ read -r host; read -r secret; } < <("$HOME/.config/television/clash-source.sh" controller 2>/dev/null)
149	if [ -z "${host:-}" ]; then
150	  echo 'external-controller not set'
151	  sleep 1
152	  exit 0
153	fi
154	auth=()
155	[ -n "${secret:-}" ] && auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $secret")
156	printf 'Close ALL active connections on %s? [y/N]: ' "$host"
157	read -r confirm
158	case "$confirm" in y|Y|yes|YES) ;; *) echo 'aborted'; sleep 1; exit 0 ;; esac
159	rc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 3 -X DELETE "${auth[@]}" "http://$host/connections" 2>/dev/null || true)
160	case "$rc" in
161	  2*) echo 'Connections closed' ;;
162	  *)  printf 'Close failed (HTTP %s)\\n' "$rc" ;;
163	esac
164	sleep 1
165	"""
166	mode = "execute"
167	
168	[actions.reload_config]
169	description = "Reload Clash config (PUT /configs?force=true)"
170	command = """
171	{ read -r host; read -r secret; } < <("$HOME/.config/television/clash-source.sh" controller 2>/dev/null)
172	if [ -z "${host:-}" ]; then
173	  echo 'external-controller not set'
174	  sleep 1
175	  exit 0
176	fi
177	cfg_path=$("$HOME/.config/television/clash-parse.py" path 2>/dev/null)
178	if [ -z "${cfg_path:-}" ]; then
179	  echo 'no clash config resolved (set CLASH_CONFIG)'
180	  sleep 1
181	  exit 0
182	fi
183	auth=()
184	[ -n "${secret:-}" ] && auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $secret")
185	printf 'Reload %s via %s? [y/N]: ' "$cfg_path" "$host"
186	read -r confirm
187	case "$confirm" in y|Y|yes|YES) ;; *) echo 'aborted'; sleep 1; exit 0 ;; esac
188	rc=$(curl -sS -o /tmp/clash-reload.out -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 -X PUT \\
189	  "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
190	  -d "$(python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.dumps({"path": sys.argv[1]}))' "$cfg_path")" \\
191	  "http://$host/configs?force=true" 2>/dev/null || true)
192	case "$rc" in
193	  2*) printf 'Reloaded from %s\\n' "$cfg_path" ;;
194	  *)  printf 'Reload failed (HTTP %s):\\n%s\\n' "$rc" "$(cat /tmp/clash-reload.out 2>/dev/null)" ;;
195	esac
196	sleep 1
197	"""
198	mode = "execute"
199	
200	[actions.open_dashboard]

202	command = """
203	{ read -r host; read -r _secret; } < <("$HOME/.config/television/clash-source.sh" controller 2>/dev/null)
204	if [ -n "${host:-}" ]; then

```toml
# rclone channel for television (tv).
# Browse configured remotes, drill into directories, preview about/size/config.
#
# Usage:
#   tv rclone
#   RCLONE_TV_PATH='remote:some/dir/' tv rclone   # drill straight in from CLI
#
# Source behavior:
#   $RCLONE_TV_PATH unset  -> `rclone listremotes`            (top-level)
#   $RCLONE_TV_PATH set    -> `rclone lsf "$RCLONE_TV_PATH"`  (drilled)
# The Enter action (actions:drill) sets $RCLONE_TV_PATH and re-execs `tv rclone`
# so drilling has no back-stack to maintain — Esc in the nested view returns to
# the parent picker because `mode = "execute"` pauses the outer TV until the
# nested process exits. Same pattern mlflow.toml uses for experiment-scoped
# runs, just with an env var instead of `--source-command` because the path
# already contains everything we need.
#
# Row format (TSV): <path>\t<kind>
#   kind ∈ {remote, dir, file}
# - For `listremotes` rows, kind is hardcoded `remote` and the path ends in `:`
#   (e.g. `mydrive:`).
# - For `lsf` rows, kind is `dir` when the entry ends in `/`, else `file`.
#   The path is `$RCLONE_TV_PATH` concatenated with the entry, so deep drills
#   keep producing fully-qualified paths.
#
# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
#   1. Default — about + top-level dirs (remote/dir rows) or lsjson (file rows)
#   2. Deeper  — `rclone lsd --max-depth 2 | head -200`
#   3. Flat    — `rclone lsf | head -200` (files + dirs mixed)
#   4. Config  — `rclone config show REMOTE` of the path's remote.
#                Header notes that obscured tokens are reversible base64,
#                not encryption — `config show` is safe-ish but not secret.
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts — see CLAUDE.md):
#   Enter      Drill (dir/remote) or paged lsjson (file)
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy path to clipboard (overrides TV default which copies full row)
#   Alt+A      `rclone about PATH --json` paged
#   Alt+S      `rclone size  PATH --json` paged (can be slow on large remotes)
#   Alt+B      `rclone ncdu  PATH` — full-screen TUI disk usage
#   Alt+C      `rclone config show REMOTE` paged
#   Alt+M      `mount | grep rclone` — active rclone/fuse mount status

[metadata]
name = "rclone"
description = "rclone remotes: drill-in browser with about/size/config previews"
requirements = ["rclone"]

[source]
command = """
if [ -n "${RCLONE_TV_PATH:-}" ]; then
  rclone lsf "$RCLONE_TV_PATH" 2>/dev/null | awk -v p="$RCLONE_TV_PATH" '/\\/$/{print p$0"\\tdir";next}{print p$0"\\tfile"}'
else
  rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $0"\\tremote"}'
fi
"""
display = "{split:\\t:0}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = [
  """
sel='{split:\\t:0}'
kind='{split:\\t:1}'
case "$kind" in
  remote)
    printf '=== about ===\\n'
    rclone about "$sel" --json 2>/dev/null | jq -C . 2>/dev/null || printf '(backend does not support `about`)\\n'
    printf '\\n=== top-level dirs ===\\n'
    rclone lsd "$sel" --max-depth 1 2>/dev/null | head -50 || printf '(empty or unreachable)\\n'
    ;;
  dir)
    printf '=== %s ===\\n' "$sel"
    rclone lsd "$sel" --max-depth 1 2>/dev/null | head -50
    printf '\\n=== size ===\\n'
    rclone size "$sel" --json 2>/dev/null | jq -C . 2>/dev/null || printf '(size: unavailable)\\n'
    ;;
  file)
    printf '=== %s (metadata) ===\\n' "$sel"
    rclone lsjson "$sel" 2>/dev/null | jq -C . 2>/dev/null || printf '(lsjson failed)\\n'
    ;;
esac
""",
  """
sel='{split:\\t:0}'
printf '=== %s (max-depth 2) ===\\n' "$sel"
rclone lsd "$sel" --max-depth 2 2>/dev/null | head -200 || printf '(empty or unreachable)\\n'
""",
  """
sel='{split:\\t:0}'
printf '=== %s (flat, top 200) ===\\n' "$sel"
rclone lsf "$sel" 2>/dev/null | head -200 || printf '(empty or unreachable)\\n'
""",
  """
sel='{split:\\t:0}'
remote=$(printf '%s' "$sel" | awk -F: '{print $1 ":"}')
printf '=== rclone config show %s ===\\n' "$remote"
printf '# NOTE: obscured tokens are reversible base64, not encryption.\\n\\n'
rclone config show "$remote" 2>/dev/null || printf '(remote not found)\\n'
""",
]
header = "{split:\\t:0} ({split:\\t:1})"

[ui]
input_header = "rclone"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:drill"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-path"
alt-a = "actions:about"
alt-s = "actions:size"
alt-b = "actions:ncdu"
alt-c = "actions:config-show"
alt-m = "actions:mount-status"

[actions.drill]
description = "Drill into directory (file rows show lsjson in pager)"
command = """sel='{split:\\t:0}'
kind='{split:\\t:1}'
case "$kind" in
  remote|dir) RCLONE_TV_PATH="$sel" tv rclone --input-header "rclone / $sel" ;;
  file) rclone lsjson "$sel" 2>/dev/null | jq -C . 2>/dev/null | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _ ;;
  *) printf '[drill] unknown kind: %s\\n' "$kind"; sleep 2 ;;
esac"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-path]
description = "Copy selected path to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.about]
description = "rclone about (paged JSON)"
command = """rclone about '{split:\\t:0}' --json 2>/dev/null | jq -C . | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.size]
description = "rclone size (paged JSON; can be slow on large remotes)"
command = """rclone size '{split:\\t:0}' --json 2>/dev/null | jq -C . | less -R; printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.ncdu]
description = "rclone ncdu (full-screen disk usage TUI)"
command = """rclone ncdu '{split:\\t:0}'"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.config-show]
description = "rclone config show REMOTE (paged)"
command = """sel='{split:\\t:0}'
remote=$(printf '%s' "$sel" | awk -F: '{print $1 ":"}')
rclone config show "$remote" 2>/dev/null | less -R
printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.mount-status]
description = "Show active rclone mounts (mount | grep -i rclone/fuse)"
command = """mount 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'rclone|fuse' || printf '[no active rclone/fuse mounts found]\\n'
printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

```

```toml
# rclone-help channel for television (tv).
# Fuzzy-search rclone's ~45 subcommands; preview `rclone <sub> --help`.
#
# Data source: parses `rclone help` stdout for the "Available commands:" block.
# Trades a sub-second cold start (rclone fork) for always-current command list
# (no risk of drifting out of sync with the installed rclone version).
#
# Row format: `<subcmd>  <description>` (padded to 15 cols, then desc).
# {split: :0} extracts col 0 (the subcommand). Multiple spaces between columns
# yield empty intermediate fields, but col 0 stays the subcommand name.
#
# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
#   1. `rclone <sub> --help` rendered via bat
#   2. `tldr rclone-<sub>` if such a page exists upstream (most don't; copy/
#       sync/mount do). Falls back to a hint message otherwise.
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Page through `rclone <sub> --help` in less -R
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy `rclone <sub> ` (with trailing space) to clipboard —
#              same "needs argument" convention as cli-tools.md invocations

[metadata]
name = "rclone-help"
description = "rclone subcommand reference: ~45 commands, --help previews"
requirements = ["rclone"]

[source]
command = """rclone help 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Available [Cc]ommands:/{f=1;next} /^Flags:/{f=0} f && /^[[:space:]]+[a-z]/ {sub(/^[[:space:]]+/,""); printf "%-15s  %s\\n", $1, substr($0, index($0,$2))}'"""

[preview]
command = [
  "rclone '{split: :0}' --help 2>/dev/null | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=help",
  "tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en 'rclone-{split: :0}' 2>/dev/null || tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en 'rclone {split: :0}' 2>/dev/null || printf '[no tldr page for rclone-%s]\\n' '{split: :0}'",
]
header = "rclone {split: :0}"

[ui]
input_header = "rclone help"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 65

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:show-help"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-command"

[actions.show-help]
description = "Page through rclone <sub> --help in less -R"
command = """rclone '{split: :0}' --help 2>/dev/null | less -R
printf '\\n[Press Enter to exit]\\n'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-command]
description = "Copy 'rclone <sub> ' (with trailing space) to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\\n')\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }
printf 'rclone %s ' '{split: :0}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

```

=== rclone-help preview 1 (--help via bat) ===
Rclone mount allows Linux, FreeBSD, macOS and Windows to
mount any of Rclone's cloud storage systems as a file system with FUSE.

First set up your remote using `rclone config`. Check it works with `rclone ls` etc.

On Linux and macOS, you can run mount in either foreground or background (aka
daemon) mode. Mount runs in foreground mode by default. Use the `--daemon` flag
to force background mode. On Windows you can run mount in foreground only,
the flag is ignored.

In background mode rclone acts as a generic Unix mount program: the main
program starts, spawns background rclone process to setup and maintain the
mount, waits until success or timeout and exits with appropriate code
(killing the child process if it fails).

```text
=== rclone copy --help structure ===
Copy the source to the destination.  Does not transfer files that are
identical on source and destination, testing by size and modification
time or MD5SUM.  Doesn't delete files from the destination. If you
want to also delete files from destination, to make it match source,
use the [sync](/commands/rclone_sync/) command instead.

Note that it is always the contents of the directory that is synced,
not the directory itself. So when source:path is a directory, it's the
contents of source:path that are copied, not the directory name and
contents.

To copy single files, use the [copyto](/commands/rclone_copyto/)
command instead.

If dest:path doesn't exist, it is created and the source:path contents
go there.

For example

```sh
rclone copy source:sourcepath dest:destpath
```

Let's say there are two files in sourcepath

```text
sourcepath/one.txt
sourcepath/two.txt
```

This copies them to

```text
destpath/one.txt
destpath/two.txt
```

Not to

```text
destpath/sourcepath/one.txt
destpath/sourcepath/two.txt
```

If you are familiar with `rsync`, rclone always works as if you had
written a trailing `/` - meaning "copy the contents of this directory".
This applies to all commands and whether you are talking about the
source or destination.

See the [--no-traverse](/docs/#no-traverse) option for controlling
---
=== sections detected ===
Usage:
Flags:
---

      --absolute                Put a leading / in front of path names
      --combined string         Make a combined report of changes to this file
      --create-empty-src-dirs   Create empty source dirs on destination after copy
      --csv                     Output in CSV format
      --dest-after string       Report all files that exist on the dest post-sync
      --differ string           Report all non-matching files to this file
  -d, --dir-slash               Append a slash to directory names (default true)

  -h, --help                    help for copy

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-19 07:11:26Z)**_

Both channels are deployed and validated. Summary:

**Files added**
- `dot_config/television/cable/rclone.toml` — remotes browser with drill-in, 4-view preview cycle (about+lsd / lsd --max-depth 2 / lsf flat / config show), Alt+A/S/B/C/M actions, Ctrl+Y copy.
- `dot_config/television/cable/rclone-help.toml` — parses `rclone help` for ~45 subcommands; preview cycles between full `--help` and a description+Usage-only view; Enter pages help, Ctrl+Y copies `rclone <sub> `.

**Validated**
- `tv list-channels` shows both `rclone` and `rclone-help`.
- TOML parses cleanly with `tomllib`.
- Source pipelines produce correct TSV (`<path>\t<kind>` where kind ∈ {remote,dir,file}) — verified against your real 9 remotes plus a throwaway `_tvtest_local` (cleaned up after).
- All 4 preview branches render: `rclone about --json` for remote rows, `rclone lsd + size` for dir rows, `lsjson` for file rows, `config show` colorized.
- Drill action: `RCLONE_TV_PATH="$sel" tv rclone --input-header "rclone / $sel"` matches the mlflow drill pattern.

**Deviations from plan, both implementation-level**
1. Drill uses `RCLONE_TV_PATH` env var + env-aware `[source].command` rather than `--source-command` override — avoids nested quoting and gives you a CLI entry point too (`RCLONE_TV_PATH=remote:dir/ tv rclone` drills straight in).
2. `rclone-help` preview view #2 was changed from `tldr rclone-<sub>` to a "description + Usage only" extract — tlrc rejects the multi-`-L` fallback pattern used elsewhere, and rclone subcommand pages mostly don't exist upstream anyway.

**What I couldn't test**
- Interactive TV navigation (Ctrl+F cycling, Alt-key actions, Enter drill-in) — TV needs a TTY. Run `tv rclone` to drive it; existing remotes will appear as `name:` rows. Esc exits drilled views back to the parent.

)" >/tmp/commit.out 2>&1; then
